amr-kernel|conf/sc/FernandoNHZSGB22.regime: wavelet-AMR BSSN finite-difference update, binary-black-hole q1/q2/q4 configs, GPU+CPU
amr-kernel|conf/sc/FernandoNHZSGB22.rationale: Dendro-GR is the sole and direct basis for both AMR variants (exact q1/q2/q4 and BSSN_MAXDEPTH parameter matches); the paper reports a single-A100 800 GFlops/s number, confirming a single-GPU path.

ann-search|conf/ics/GengYLWZ26.regime: MRI/GIS/PLY real 2D-3D point clouds treated as k-NN queries (RT-core accelerated)
ann-search|conf/ics/GengYLWZ26.rationale: X-HD's own deliverable is a Hausdorff-distance VALUE (a max-min reduction over k-NN results), which the spec explicitly puts out of scope for the ann-search variants — only its internal k-NN routine is a valid submission; its real point-cloud domains are, however, literally folded into the exact-spatial-knn-kernel suite.

ann-search|conf/ics/KamelYC25.regime: exact GPU k-NN via spatio-graph hubs+lower-bounds, synthetic uniform 3D points + real mesh point clouds
ann-search|conf/ics/KamelYC25.rationale: CLOVER is the direct source of the exact-spatial-knn-kernel variant — its own dataset sizes/dimensions are copied into the spec's recommended_subset and its correctness gaps (dead-code check) are what the spec's mandatory correctness requirement fixes.

ann-search|conf/ppopp/000122.regime: RT-core-mapped exact/bounded-approximate low-dim (3D) neighbor search on KITTI/Stanford-3D/Millennium-N-body
ann-search|conf/ppopp/000122.rationale: RTNN's three real domains are directly incorporated into the exact-spatial-knn-kernel variant's recommended_subset and its measured-error-rate practice for approximate radius relaxation is adopted as the spec's own reporting requirement.

ann-search|conf/sc/ChenH0LYDY000025.regime: IVF-PQ ANNS on SIFT/DEEP/SPACEV at 1B and 100M scale, 10K queries, recall@10>=0.8 floor
ann-search|conf/sc/ChenH0LYDY000025.rationale: DRIM-ANN is one of the 4 primary high-dim papers whose SIFT/DEEP/SPACEV suite the spec's recommended_subset is built from directly, but it runs on UPMEM DRAM-PIM hardware, not a GPU.

ann-search|conf/sc/ChenZSLY25.regime: PIM billion-scale ANNS with early-pruning top-k, same SIFT/DEEP/SPACEV suite as DRIM-ANN
ann-search|conf/sc/ChenZSLY25.rationale: UpANNS is one of the 4 primary high-dim papers sharing the exact SIFT/DEEP/SPACEV suite the spec standardizes on, but it runs on PIM hardware ('other' platform), not a single GPU.

ann-search|conf/sc/JiangLZLHSRZRHA23.regime: FPGA hardware-algorithm co-design auto-generating vector-search accelerators for user-given recall targets, SIFT/Deep100M
ann-search|conf/sc/JiangLZLHSRZRHA23.rationale: FANNS has the most complete recall-Pareto framing of any surveyed paper and is the direct model for the spec's recall@{1,10,100}-vs-QPS metric and batch/single-query latency-distribution requirement, but it targets FPGA, not GPU.

ann-search|conf/usenix/KimPNHKLL25.regime: graph-based (CAGRA) approximate NN search, SIFT-128-euclidean, mean-recall@10 + median-latency per swept config
ann-search|conf/usenix/KimPNHKLL25.rationale: PathWeaver is one of the 4 primary high-dim papers this spec's Pareto-recall/QPS variant is built around; although its headline 3.24x claim requires 4 GPUs+NVLink, the spec's own open_questions confirm a single-GPU harness script (single_pathweaver_one.py) exists and was read.

astar-search|conf/ics/Al-KhansaGMH26.regime: single-pair 8-connected occupancy-grid A* search, GPU-parallel bidirectional bucketed priority structure, single NVIDIA GPU
astar-search|conf/ics/Al-KhansaGMH26.rationale: This is the sole surveyed paper and the direct basis for both spec variants (MovingAI-benchmark search-phase throughput and the paper's own procedural-grid generator sweep); headline is the parallel bidirectional A* algorithm itself.

attention-kernel|conf/asplos/TangLWSLXZL.regime: MHA/MLA shapes (BERT/ViT/LLaMA-65B/DeepSeek-R1), fp, GPU (A10/H800 per survey)
attention-kernel|conf/asplos/TangLWSLXZL.rationale: RedFuser is a general cascaded-reduction fusion compiler; attention (softmax+GEMM) is one of several fused patterns alongside MoE routing and FP8-quantized GEMM, matching the compiler/DSL-generates-this-kernel-among-others definition, though its named MHA/MLA sources match the spec's prefill regime well.

attention-kernel|conf/asplos/YiZHYSWZZLL.regime: paged fp16 KV cache decode attention, GQA-heavy, saturating batch sizes, GPU
attention-kernel|conf/asplos/YiZHYSWZZLL.rationale: PAT's headline is exactly a prefix-aware decode-attention kernel; the spec's attn-decode-kv-cache-kernel variant is built directly around PAT's own claim and shapes.

attention-kernel|conf/cgo/ZhangDSHSP26.regime: MHA prefill (batch1/heads32/d64/seq2048) and flash-decoding shapes, fp, GPU
attention-kernel|conf/cgo/ZhangDSHSP26.rationale: Hexcute is a general GPU-layout-synthesis compiler; attention is one of four benchmarked kernel classes (GEMM, Attention, FP8 GEMM, warp-specialized) plus MoE/Mamba, but its own benchmark_attention.py shapes are explicitly named as defining the spec's prefill-kernel suite.

attention-kernel|conf/ics/FuYDS24.regime: full-sequence self-attention, fp32, ARM multi-core CPU
attention-kernel|conf/ics/FuYDS24.rationale: MEATTEN is the track's sole CPU paper and directly defines the spec's attn-cpu-kernel-multicore variant.

attention-kernel|conf/ipps/ZhaiJWJZCLZ23.regime: BERT-style bidirectional MHA, variable-length/padding-free, fp, GPU
attention-kernel|conf/ipps/ZhaiJWJZCLZ23.rationale: ByteTransformer's headline is a padding-free fused MHA kernel evaluated against PyTorch at kernel level; its BERT-base sweep directly defines part of the spec's prefill-kernel input suite.

attention-kernel|conf/ppopp/ChenC0XMM0X0.regime: unified attention across FlashAttention-style algorithm variants, NVIDIA+AMD GPU
attention-kernel|conf/ppopp/ChenC0XMM0X0.rationale: MetaAttention's sole target is attention-kernel generation across hardware backends (not a multi-kernel-class compiler like RedFuser/Hexcute), evaluated at kernel level against FlashAttention on both NVIDIA and AMD.

attention-kernel|conf/ppopp/Xu0BXX00000C.regime: fused GEMM+softmax attention, tensor-vector parallelism, GPU
attention-kernel|conf/ppopp/Xu0BXX00000C.rationale: FlashAttention-T's headline is exactly a fully-tensorized fused attention kernel evaluated against FlashAttention baselines at kernel level; explicitly named in the spec.

attention-kernel|conf/sc/ChenHPLG0D021.rationale: E.T.'s headline includes a re-engineered self-attention operator (plus a separate pruning contribution) evaluated against TensorRT/FasterTransformer; one of the 9 papers the spec was directly built from.

attention-kernel|conf/sc/WangWXHQDWL22.regime: fp16/int8 Transformer training kernels (embeddings, layers, attention), GPU
attention-kernel|conf/sc/WangWXHQDWL22.rationale: LightSeq2 optimizes the whole Transformer training pipeline (embeddings, encoder/decoder, attention, etc.); attention is one of many fused kernels and evaluation is end-to-end training speedup, not an isolated attention-kernel throughput number.

autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/asplos/Ikara.regime: 80+ hand-scheduled BLAS/GEMM kernels via a user-extensible scheduling language, CPU/ARM, no confirmed search-cost or correctness protocol
autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/asplos/Ikara.rationale: Exo 2 is a scheduling-language autotuning system generating high-performance kernels including GEMM/BLAS, but survey.md notes this is the lowest-confidence entry (abstract-only) and its evaluation is expert-schedule-driven rather than the suite's fixed kernel set with a reported search/tuning cost.

autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/asplos/Qiao0.regime: LLM/DNN operator kernels (matmul, conv, attention) fp32/fp16 on NVIDIA GPUs, jointly-reported search-cost-vs-performance curve
autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/asplos/Qiao0.rationale: Explicitly named in the spec as the clearest example of jointly reporting search cost and achieved kernel performance; its LLM-kernel workloads match the suite's gemm_llm_ffn/batched_attention entries.

autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/asplos/WonME.regime: SpMV/SpMM/SDDMM/MTTKRP over 726 generated sparsity patterns on CPU, search/tuning cost unreported despite being the paper's core contribution
autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/asplos/WonME.rationale: WACO's kernel types (SpMM/SDDMM/MTTKRP) overlap the suite but its 726-pattern corpus differs from the suite's fixed matrices, and survey.md flags that WACO's core ANN-search cost is never quantified despite being explicitly named in the spec as a track gap.

autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/asplos/YeLSC.regime: SpMM/SDDMM/sparse attention/sparse conv on GNN graphs (Cora/CiteSeer/PubMed/OGB/Reddit) on NVIDIA GPUs, rigorous 10-100-warmup/100-rep protocol
autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/asplos/YeLSC.rationale: SparseTIR's SpMM/SDDMM workloads directly match the suite's spmm/sddmm entries (same GNN-graph convention as benchspecs/spmm); its own search-cost amortization is only argued qualitatively, not quantified.

autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/asplos/Zheng.regime: GEMM/conv/tensor-contraction kernels across GPU/FPGA/CPU vendor-library comparisons
autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/asplos/Zheng.rationale: FlexTensor's GEMM/conv targets match the suite's gemm_square/conv2d_resnet50 entries; explicitly named in the spec as one of the papers reporting post-tuning numbers with no bounded search budget.

autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/cgo/HeY25.regime: fused LLM kernels (feed-forward, matmul, batched matmul, flash-attention) fp16 on a single A100, search cost reported separately as one-time RL training cost
autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/cgo/HeY25.rationale: Explicitly named in the spec text; its LLM-kernel targets match the suite's gemm_llm_ffn/batched_attention framing and it reports tuning cost (RL training time) separately from throughput as the spec requires.

autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/cgo/IvanovZD.regime: Rodinia benchmark-suite mini-apps (BFS, hotspot, LUD, etc.), cross-vendor NVIDIA/AMD GPU granularity autotuning
autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/cgo/IvanovZD.rationale: The autotuning/retargeting compiler is squarely the group's kind of system, but its evaluated suite (Rodinia mini-apps) is a completely different benchmark set from the spec's dense/sparse tensor-kernel or PolyBench suites.

autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/cgo/LopezKB2.regime: symbolic-size BLAS/LAPACK matrix-chain sequencing, CPU, no reported search-budget
autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/cgo/LopezKB2.rationale: GMC is a compiler system selecting BLAS/LAPACK kernel-call sequences, matching the group's own definition, but it optimizes matrix CHAINS rather than the fixed suite's single dense/sparse kernels and reports no search-cost number (explicitly flagged in survey.md as a track gap).

autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/ipps/Georgan.regime: GEMM/MLP/ResNet-50-conv/block-sparse-matmul kernels on CPU, explicit wall-time tuning-cost comparison vs TVM-Ansor
autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/ipps/Georgan.rationale: Explicitly named in the spec as reporting search cost in wall time; its GEMM/conv kernels match the suite's gemm_square/conv2d_resnet50 entries.

autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/ipps/LiuDYC0.regime: DNN operator kernels (Conv2d/GEMM/GEMV/AvgPool) on cloud/edge NVIDIA GPUs, compile time and FLOPS reported in separate figures, not jointly
autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/ipps/LiuDYC0.rationale: Gensor's GEMM/Conv2d configs overlap the suite but GEMV/AvgPool do not, and per survey.md it reports search/compile time and steady-state performance in separate figures rather than a joint Pareto curve.

autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/ppopp/XuSZLH.regime: PolyBench/C affine kernels (nussinov, fdtd-2d, heat-3d, seidel-2d, etc.), precision-vs-speed frontier, CPU+GPU
autotuner-multi-kernel|conf/ppopp/XuSZLH.rationale: The spec's polybench-affine-mixed-precision variant is built directly and explicitly around PrecTuner's own confirmed test set.

batched-gemm|conf/ics/0001SLFY024.regime: variable-shape/segmented GEMM on 8 real heterogeneous-graph relation-type distributions, NVIDIA GPU
batched-gemm|conf/ics/0001SLFY024.rationale: FASTEN's headline IS the segmented-GEMM kernel, matching the spec's batched-gemm-variable-kernel variant exactly, but the spec notes its own uniform-shape variant is 'not directly evidenced by FASTEN's own artifact.'

betweenness|conf/ppopp/Shun20.regime: real-world hypergraphs, shared-memory 72-core CPU, hypergraph betweenness centrality is one of ~8 algorithms (also MIS, k-core, hypertrees, hyperpaths, connected components, PageRank, SSSP) in an exte
betweenness|conf/ppopp/Shun20.rationale: Shun20 does implement genuine parallel hypergraph BC (Brandes-style, matching the spec's semantics), but it is one algorithm among a broad general-purpose hypergraph-processing framework, not the paper's singular headline contribution.

bfs|conf/ics/ElbekK26.regime: real-world graphs, GPU tensor-core-accelerated pull-based BFS, vs Gunrock/GSWITCH/BerryBees
bfs|conf/ics/ElbekK26.rationale: BLEST's headline IS a BFS algorithm/implementation evaluated directly against BFS baselines on real-world graphs.

bfs|conf/ics/NeffZMHTKB24.regime: probabilistic (stochastic edge-weighted) breadth-first traversals for influence-maximization Monte-Carlo sampling, AMD GPU + distributed (Frontier)
bfs|conf/ics/NeffZMHTKB24.rationale: Per survey.md, this is 'not a plain-BFS paper' -- probabilistic traversal is a materially different kernel from deterministic reachability BFS, embedded as the sampling step of an influence-maximization application; platform is AMD GPU/distributed, not a single NVIDIA GPU.

bfs|conf/ipps/ChenSSTBL22.regime: bit-level B2SR SpMV/SpGEMM GraphBLAS primitives; BFS is a composed downstream application, not directly measured in the reachable artifact (only the BMV microbenchmark is)
bfs|conf/ipps/ChenSSTBL22.rationale: Per survey.md, the public artifact ships only the underlying Boolean matrix-vector-multiply microbenchmark; BFS-specific numbers are an abstract-level composed claim ('GraphBLAS-based BFS accelerate up to 433x'), not a directly benchmarked kernel.

bfs|conf/ipps/GeraK23.regime: Elias-Fano compressed real-world graphs on GPU; BFS is one of three downstream applications (BFS/SSSP/PageRank) of a novel compression format
bfs|conf/ipps/GeraK23.rationale: Headline contribution is the graph-compression format; BFS is one of three applications used to demonstrate its benefit rather than the paper's own optimized kernel.

bfs|conf/ipps/MlakarWPS21.regime: GPU/CPU speculative parallel bandwidth-reducing reordering, downstream BFS/SpMV benefit
bfs|conf/ipps/MlakarWPS21.rationale: Explicitly named alongside Corder in the spec's bfs-reordering-cost variant as a reordering-focused anchor paper.

bfs|conf/sc/AraiNITUYSF24.regime: Graph500 R-MAT/Kronecker graphs, distributed BFS at Fugaku-class SCALE, ARM CPU
bfs|conf/sc/AraiNITUYSF24.rationale: Headline IS Graph500-benchmark BFS performance; the spec explicitly notes SCALE>=38 Fugaku-class as reportable. No GPU (ARM CPU, distributed).

bfs|journals/tpds/ChenC22.regime: cache-aware graph reordering evaluated via downstream BFS/PageRank/etc. on 7 large real graphs, CPU
bfs|journals/tpds/ChenC22.rationale: Corder is explicitly named in the spec's bfs-reordering-cost variant ('gives reordering-focused papers (Corder, RCM) a variant that measures what they actually contribute').

bipartite-matching|conf/ipps/AkathoottB2.regime: 21-instance SuiteSparse suite (from the paper's own README), GPU bidirectional augmenting-path matching
bipartite-matching|conf/ipps/AkathoottB2.rationale: The entire spec's 21-graph suite is adopted verbatim from ECL-MM's own README.

blas-level1-2|conf/asplos/ChenMCA21.regime: non-SIMD vectorizer generator; dot product (uint8 x int8 -> int32, native VNNI instruction width) is one of several target kernels and is the paper's own basis for the mixed-precision-reduction varian
blas-level1-2|conf/asplos/ChenMCA21.rationale: VeGen's own `dot_16x1x16_uint8_int8_int32` kernel is the literal basis for the spec's blas-l1-mixed-precision-reduction variant, but the spec explicitly notes VeGen's own evaluation is a static instruction-count comparison rather than the measured wall-clock throughput the variant requires -- a genuine evaluation-protocol gap, not just an input-regime one.

blas-level1-2|conf/asplos/IkarashiQDRBR2.regime: general user-extensible scheduling language generating 80+ high-performance kernels across domains; BLAS-L1/L2-shaped kernels are among the broader set, exact op list and sizes unconfirmed, CPU/ARM
blas-level1-2|conf/asplos/IkarashiQDRBR2.rationale: Exo 2 is a general USL/codegen framework (a compiler that generates this kernel among others), explicitly named as a target for the spec's blas-l1l2-generated-kernel-suite variant, but the spec itself flags the exact BLAS op list as an open question.

blas-level1-2|conf/cgo/PatelAA25.regime: symmetric sparse/dense tensor compiler generating symmetry-aware kernels including SSYMV among MTTKRP and general n-dimensional symmetric tensor kernels, CPU
blas-level1-2|conf/cgo/PatelAA25.rationale: SySTeC's `ssymv` is directly named as the pairing partner for GEMV in the spec's blas-l2-gemv-symv-kernel variant, but SySTeC is a general compiler (SSYMV is one of many symmetry-aware kernels it generates) and its own SYMV problem size could not be confirmed from source.

blas-level1-2|conf/sc/MatteisLH20.regime: named BLAS L1/L2/L3 routines (dot, gemv, trsm, etc.) as a streaming HLS library, on-the-fly synthetic vectors/matrices, FPGA
blas-level1-2|conf/sc/MatteisLH20.rationale: fBLAS is the only one of the four papers in this track that benchmarks named BLAS routines directly against a reference library (the spec says so explicitly); its own sdot/ddot/sgemv/dgemv harnesses are the direct basis for both blas-l1-vector-kernel and blas-l2-gemv-symv-kernel.

cellular-automata|journals/tpds/NavarroQ.regime: Larger-Than-Life (LTL) cellular automata, radius sweep 1<=r<=16, tensor-core mapping vs CUDA-core baselines (naive/coarsened/shared-memory-tiled/bit-packed) from the same codebase
cellular-automata|journals/tpds/NavarroQ.rationale: CAT is the paper this track's spec is written around almost verbatim: a tensor-core-mapped LTL CA implementation compared against CUDA-core baselines across a radius sweep, the exact axis the spec calls out.

cg-krylov|conf/ics/ZhangWCMWEM23.regime: unpreconditioned CG kernel (SpMV + 2 dots + 3 axpys), SuiteSparse matrices (smaller and larger sets), single NVIDIA GPU, persistent-kernel execution model
cg-krylov|conf/ics/ZhangWCMWEM23.rationale: PERKS's own CG research question is quoted verbatim as the spec's cg-kernel-fixed-iter variant's defining claim ('matching PERKS's explicit research question').

cg-krylov|conf/ipps/NoackKK25.regime: DSL-generated SpMV/ILU/PBiCGStab sparse solvers on Graphcore IPUs, SuiteSparse plus synthetic Poisson matrices, MPIR+double-word arithmetic for missing native fp64
cg-krylov|conf/ipps/NoackKK25.rationale: Graphene is a general DSL/codegen framework generating a suite of linear solvers/preconditioners (SpMV, ILU, PBiCGStab), not a CG implementation; the spec explicitly excludes nonsymmetric/BiCGStab-type solves as out of scope for this CG-specific track, and the platform (IPU) is outside the benchmark's NVIDIA-GPU scope.

cg-krylov|conf/sc/BrunnHBMM20.regime: Gauss-Newton-Krylov solve embedded in a nonlinear diffeomorphic image-registration pipeline, single-V100 number reported alongside multi-GPU scaling, not a standalone SPD test-matrix solve
cg-krylov|conf/sc/BrunnHBMM20.rationale: The Krylov solve here is the inner linear-system step of an outer nonlinear Gauss-Newton optimization for image registration (a solver stack), not a direct CG-on-SPD-matrix claim comparable to the spec's SuiteSparse/HPCG-generator regime.

cg-krylov|conf/sc/MaACSH25.regime: ILU(0)/ILU(K)-preconditioned CG on SPD SuiteSparse matrices, both iterative-phase and end-to-end speedups with preconditioner setup measured and reported separately, single A100
cg-krylov|conf/sc/MaACSH25.rationale: SPCG's own artifact discipline (separating preconditioner analysis+factorization from the PCG loop) is generalized directly into the spec's cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence variant as a mandatory requirement.

cg-krylov|conf/sc/SuzukiI25.regime: nested FGMRES/Richardson Krylov solver with fp16 inner iterations, to-convergence solve on symmetric/SPD matrices overlapping the recommended subset, CPU
cg-krylov|conf/sc/SuzukiI25.rationale: F3R is one of the two papers the spec's cg-mixed-precision-cascade variant is explicitly built around ('F3R's own symmetric list already overlaps heavily with' the recommended subset); headline is the reduced-precision-cascade solver itself, evaluated to convergence.

cg-krylov|conf/sc/YangZNJS0T024.regime: tile-grained mixed-precision single-kernel CG/PCG/BiCGSTAB/PBiCGSTAB solver, single A100 and single MI210
cg-krylov|conf/sc/YangZNJS0T024.rationale: Mille-feuille is explicitly named as one of the two papers ('the two papers in this track that build reduced-precision Krylov solvers as their central contribution') the cg-mixed-precision-cascade variant targets.

cg-krylov|journals/tpds/BernaschiCVD23.regime: AMG-preconditioned Krylov solver on synthetic 3D-Laplacian stencil SPD systems, weak/strong scaling including a rank=1 single-GPU starting point, multi-GPU MPI-CUDA
cg-krylov|journals/tpds/BernaschiCVD23.rationale: BootCMatchGX's own `--laplacian-3d` generator and convergence protocol (relative residual < 1e-6, capped 1000 iterations) is quoted verbatim as the spec's cg-hpcg-generator-amg and cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence variants' basis; its own weak-scaling series starts at rank count 1, giving a genuine single-GPU data point.

cholesky|conf/ipps/CaoAPBLKD22.regime: distributed tile low-rank (TLR) Cholesky, STARS-H-generated 3D data-sparse covariance matrices, fp64
cholesky|conf/ipps/CaoAPBLKD22.rationale: Headline is runtime-level optimizations (trimming, rank-aware distribution) specifically for TLR Cholesky factorization, evaluated as factorization performance vs. other TLR Cholesky implementations; explicitly cited in the spec as 'paper 2' for the TLR variant. CPU/distributed only.

cholesky|conf/ipps/CaoPABLKD21.regime: distributed TLR Cholesky, 3D exponential Matern covariance matrices, fp64
cholesky|conf/ipps/CaoPABLKD21.rationale: Headline is PaRSEC-runtime/rank-aware optimizations specifically for TLR Cholesky factorization, evaluated as a 7x speedup over prior TLR Cholesky implementations; explicitly the spec's 'paper 5' source. CPU/distributed only.

cholesky|conf/ipps/MondalAL0GK22.regime: TLR/HODLR Cholesky-based likelihood evaluation, STARS-H covariance matrices
cholesky|conf/ipps/MondalAL0GK22.rationale: Headline is a new non-Gaussian (Tukey g-and-h) statistical model for geospatial data; TLR Cholesky is the underlying, reused ExaGeoStat-family computational engine, matching the instructions' 'geostatistics application' component example, though the input suite matches the spec's TLR variant.

cholesky|conf/sc/CaoAAPNBDGKLS22.regime: mixed-precision + low-rank tile Cholesky, STARS-H covariance matrices, Fugaku A64FX
cholesky|conf/sc/CaoAAPNBDGKLS22.rationale: Central technical contribution is combining mixed-precision and low-rank computation within one tile Cholesky solver, evaluated kernel-level (12x vs. a highly-optimized dense Cholesky baseline). No GPU (Fugaku A64FX CPU nodes).

cholesky|conf/sc/KwasniewskiKBZS21.regime: communication-optimal 2.5D dense Cholesky/LU, single-node and distributed fp64
cholesky|conf/sc/KwasniewskiKBZS21.rationale: This is the explicitly-named 'paper 1' basis for both the single-node and distributed fp64 Cholesky variants (its own NB-tuning behavior is cited as the motivating lesson); no GPU, CPU/distributed only.

cholesky|conf/sc/LtaiefACRSKDBAK24.regime: GPU tensor-core mixed-precision (FP64/FP32/FP16/INT8/FP8) tile Cholesky, real UK BioBank GWAS covariance matrices
cholesky|conf/sc/LtaiefACRSKDBAK24.rationale: The paper's headline IS a new four-precision Cholesky-based solver reaching 1.805 mixed-precision ExaOp/s; explicitly the source for the GPU/tensor-core tier of the mixed-precision variant (UK BioBank GWAS size cited directly in the spec).

cholesky|journals/tpds/AbdulahCPBDGKLS22.regime: three-precision (FP64/32/16) tile Cholesky, STARS-H covariance matrices, multi-GPU PaRSEC
cholesky|journals/tpds/AbdulahCPBDGKLS22.rationale: Headline is a three-precision tile-Cholesky/TRSM solver for Gaussian MLE via PaRSEC, matching the mixed-precision variant's 'band-percentage' scheme; kernels_assigned explicitly list Cholesky factorization and TRSM. Includes an NVIDIA-GPU platform path.

cholesky|journals/tpds/SalvanaAHLSGK21.regime: low-rank-approximated Cholesky-based Gaussian log-likelihood for multivariate geospatial cokriging
cholesky|journals/tpds/SalvanaAHLSGK21.rationale: Headline is a multivariate geospatial statistics/cokriging methodology; Cholesky-based likelihood evaluation with low-rank approximation is the reused computational engine, matching the geostatistics-application component pattern despite input-suite overlap with the spec.

climate-kernel|conf/ipps/YaoZLX26.regime: FP16 Tensor-Core shallow-water dynamical core, Williamson test suite
climate-kernel|conf/ipps/YaoZLX26.rationale: Unlike its tangential role in the gemm group, here the paper's headline (accelerating a shallow-water dynamical core) IS exactly what this track's dyncore variant measures; the variant is reused verbatim from this same paper's stencil-track entry.

climate-kernel|conf/sc/AbdulahBBCCGKKL24.regime: mixed-precision SHT + tile-low-rank Cholesky climate emulator, multi-GPU/distributed (AMD+NVIDIA)
climate-kernel|conf/sc/AbdulahBBCCGKKL24.rationale: This paper's own training data and 0.976 EFlop/s Frontier-scale headline point are the explicit, sole basis for the climate-emulator-solver-kernel variant. Runs on NVIDIA GPUs (Alps GH200, Leonardo A100) among other platforms.

community-detection|conf/ipps/NiuOSC26.regime: Louvain modularity-maximizing community detection with convergence guarantee, CPU, SNAP graphs
community-detection|conf/ipps/NiuOSC26.rationale: NiuOSC26 is explicitly named as the subject matter operationalized by the cd-determinism-repeatability variant and is a source for cd-kernel-modularity; headline IS the Louvain algorithm itself. CPU only.

community-detection|conf/ppopp/WangLLWM0.regime: GPU-accelerated Louvain modularity community detection, SNAP graphs
community-detection|conf/ppopp/WangLLWM0.rationale: GALA's headline IS a GPU Louvain algorithm; its own README com-lj worked example is explicitly reproduced verbatim in the cd-kernel-modularity variant's recommended subset.

community-detection|conf/sc/BestaMLTIKAJ.rationale: ProbGraph's clustering algorithm is explicitly named as the basis for the alt-objective (non-modularity) variant of this track; clustering is one of the two headline applications of the paper's core technique. CPU only.

community-detection|journals/tpds/ZhuSFX.regime: structural-information-theory (non-modularity) community detection, hybrid sparse CPU/GPU
community-detection|journals/tpds/ZhuSFX.rationale: HSSInfo's headline IS a community detection algorithm (structural-entropy minimization), explicitly named as the basis for the cd-alt-objective-report variant; evaluated kernel-level against eleven baseline algorithms.

connected-components|conf/ipps/SahuARKB2.regime: 30 real-world graphs, GPU biconnected components, both in-memory and out-of-core (edge-pruning skeleton)
connected-components|conf/ipps/SahuARKB2.rationale: Headline IS a GPU BCC algorithm with dedicated in-memory and out-of-core variants, matching the spec's cc-bcc-kernel-inmemory and cc-bcc-oom-external variants exactly.

connected-components|conf/ppopp/DongW002.regime: graphs of varying diameter (including large-diameter road-network-like graphs), CPU parallel biconnected components
connected-components|conf/ppopp/DongW002.rationale: Headline IS a space-efficient parallel BCC algorithm improving on Tarjan-Vishkin/BFS approaches, matching the spec's BCC in-memory variant (CPU side).

connected-components|conf/sc/AlabandiSBB.regime: power-law graphs and near-constant-degree mesh graphs (radiative transfer), GPU, A100
connected-components|conf/sc/AlabandiSBB.rationale: Headline IS a GPU strongly-connected-components algorithm, matching the spec's dedicated cc-scc-kernel variant.

connected-components|journals/tpds/Alleg.regime: 2D and 3D binary image datasets (real + synthetic), GPU 8-connectivity labeling, YACCLAB benchmark
connected-components|journals/tpds/Alleg.rationale: Headline IS a GPU 2D/3D connected-component-labeling algorithm on regular image grids, matching the spec's dedicated cc-image-ccl-2d3d variant exactly.

content-defined-chunking|journals/tpds/U.regime: SIMD-vectorized content-defined chunking, DEB real VM-image dataset, CPU
content-defined-chunking|journals/tpds/U.rationale: SeqCDC is the sole and direct basis for this track's only variant (matching '10x over unaccelerated' claim verbatim). CPU (SSE/AVX) only, no GPU.

convolution|conf/asplos/0033XSRS21.regime: dense conv2d layer shapes from ResNet-18/YOLO/MobileNet-depthwise (the exact shape lists the spec's suite is built from), fp32, multicore CPU, per-iteration cache-flushed timing
convolution|conf/asplos/0033XSRS21.rationale: This paper's own resnet.txt/yolo.txt/deepwise.txt layer-shape files are the literal source of the spec's conv-dense-kernel-fp32 recommended_subset; headline is a loop-tiling analytical model evaluated at kernel level against oneDNN/AutoTVM.

convolution|conf/asplos/ChenMCA21.regime: non-SIMD vectorizer generator targeting DSP/image/ML kernels; convolution is one of several target kernels, its specific workload/shape details not independently confirmed, CPU
convolution|conf/asplos/ChenMCA21.rationale: Per survey.md, 'convolution is not [VeGen's] primary or sole subject the way it is for [the other convolution-track] papers' -- it is peripheral evidence for a general vectorizer-generator, fitting the compiler-generates-this-kernel-among-others component case, but with real uncertainty about how closely its conv target matches the spec's shape suite.

convolution|conf/asplos/DingYZLWP23.regime: general DL tensor-program task-mapping compiler for GPU and TPU (GEMM, conv, and other operators); claims inference latency rivaling cuDNN/cuBLAS but exact conv workload/shapes unconfirmed (abstract-l
convolution|conf/asplos/DingYZLWP23.rationale: Hidet generates many different tensor-program kernel types via a task-mapping paradigm, so conv is one of several outputs (component), but survey.md could not confirm its specific conv evaluation protocol/shapes beyond the abstract's general claim.

convolution|conf/cgo/CowanMCBC20.regime: sub-8-bit/binary quantized ResNet-18 layer-by-layer convolution (1x1/1x2/2x2 weight/activation-bit precisions), ARM CPU (Raspberry Pi 3B+)
convolution|conf/cgo/CowanMCBC20.rationale: This paper's own ResNet-18 layer-by-layer benchmark at ultra-low-bit precision is reused verbatim as the spec's conv-quantized-kernel variant's suite; it also cleanly separates kernel-only timing from end-to-end and from one-shot micro-kernel synthesis cost.

convolution|conf/dac/BasalamaWC23.regime: HLS systolic-array design-space search for GEMM+conv layers sampled from VGG16/MobileNetV2/ResNet50/ResNet152, HLS-estimated cycle/latency/resource cost model rather than a measured wall-clock kernel
convolution|conf/dac/BasalamaWC23.rationale: Odyssey is a DSE tool spanning both matmul and conv kernels (component); per survey.md its own run_tests.py entry point is a synthesis-model search, not a profiled kernel execution, which is a categorically different measurement paradigm from this spec's GFLOP/s kernel variants.

convolution|conf/ics/LiXSS24.regime: TVM/Ansor autotuning-search-cost reduction for GEMM+conv2d task sets (YOLO/ResNet networks), RTX3090/4090; found kernel quality matches, not beats, vanilla Ansor by design
convolution|conf/ics/LiXSS24.rationale: Ansor-AF-DS is a general autotuner covering both GEMM and conv2d (a compiler that generates this kernel among others), so conv is one of two target ops; its actual contribution -- reaching the same code quality in far fewer trials -- is exactly the spec's dedicated conv-tuning-cost variant, which the spec built around this paper.

convolution|conf/ipps/WangFD21.regime: sliding-channel convolution (a novel grouped-conv variant) evaluated only via a full 350-epoch PyTorch CIFAR-10 training loop (loss/accuracy progress bar), no isolated forward-conv kernel timing harne
convolution|conf/ipps/WangFD21.rationale: Per survey.md, DSXplore's repo has no isolated forward-conv-only timing harness -- the paper's claimed kernel-level speedups are not reproducible from the artifact without extracting and separately benchmarking the SCC op, so despite a genuinely novel kernel design the actual evaluation regime is end-to-end training, not kernel-level.

convolution|conf/ppopp/LiuZYLQ24.regime: pruned sparse conv layers extracted from VGG19/ResNet50/YOLOv3/MobileNet checkpoints at multiple sparsity levels, fp32, single V100
convolution|conf/ppopp/LiuZYLQ24.rationale: Tetris's own benchmark methodology (take a base dense CNN layer, prune it, time the pruned shape) is quoted verbatim as the spec's conv-sparse-pruned-kernel-fp32 variant's methodology.

convolution|journals/tpds/LiS21.regime: 1-bit XNOR bit-Tensor-Core convolution/GEMM; headline metric is end-to-end ResNet-18 ImageNet throughput (images/sec), not per-layer kernel GFLOP/s, Turing GPU
convolution|journals/tpds/LiS21.rationale: Per survey.md, TC-BNN's headline number is whole-network images/sec (5.6K img/s), explicitly noted as an end-to-end rather than kernel-only data point despite bit-convolution being the paper's central kernel design.

dnn-operator-fusion|conf/asplos/TangLWSL.regime: automatic fusion of cascaded reductions (softmax+GEMM, MHA/MLA, MoE routing, FP8-quant-GEMM) into single kernels
dnn-operator-fusion|conf/asplos/TangLWSL.rationale: RedFuser is one of the two primary evidence papers this spec is built around, reported at exactly the subgraph granularity the fusion-subgraph variant measures, with 4 of its own pattern types (MHA/MLA/MoE-routing/FP8-quant-GEMM) forming the variant's pattern set.

dnn-operator-fusion|conf/cgo/LopoukhineF.regime: unconfirmed — MLIR compiler backend for RISC-V streaming-register accelerator generating unspecified DNN micro-kernels
dnn-operator-fusion|conf/cgo/LopoukhineF.rationale: The spec's own notes_on_fairness admits this paper 'only fits the taxonomy' at one corner and contributes no concrete numeric defaults; its listed artifact repo turned out to be an unrelated protobuf-acceleration project, so no fusion-specific behavior, shapes, or baselines could be confirmed at all, and its platform is a non-GPU RISC-V accelerator.

dnn-operator-fusion|conf/ics/PrabhakarK0.regime: unconfirmed — weight-repetition factorization/memoization inside a single quantized conv/GEMM kernel on CPU
dnn-operator-fusion|conf/ics/PrabhakarK0.rationale: The spec's own evidence entry states this is 'not a multi-op fusion chain' but a single-kernel redundancy-elimination technique, and calls the paper abstract-only with an empty-stub artifact and a paywalled PDF, so it barely fits the operator-fusion definition this track measures.

dnn-operator-fusion|conf/ppopp/DaiDRYLL0.regime: sparse-attention kernels plus searched fusion templates across kernel, subgraph, e2e-model, and tuning-time granularities
dnn-operator-fusion|conf/ppopp/DaiDRYLL0.rationale: STOF is the other primary evidence paper; its own three benchmark scripts (kernel-level 10/20, end-to-end 10/10, and its Table 4 search-time comparison) map one-to-one onto the spec's fusion-single-kernel, fusion-e2e-model, and fusion-compile-search-time variants.

dnn-operator-fusion|conf/sc/WangWXHQDWL2.regime: GPU kernel fusion for Transformer training (operator-level + full-training-model-level), V100/A100
dnn-operator-fusion|conf/sc/WangWXHQDWL2.rationale: LightSeq2 is one of the two hand-written reference papers the spec's fusion-e2e-model variant is modeled on, reporting both an operator-level granularity (e.g. LayerNorm ~4x) and a full-training-model-level number exactly as the variant requires.

dp-dynamic-programming|conf/ics/YangLWHT.regime: large sparse real-world graphs, hybrid Floyd-Warshall+Dijkstra APSP, distributed multi-GPU
dp-dynamic-programming|conf/ics/YangLWHT.rationale: This is the sole paper the dp-dynamic-programming spec was built around -- its Floyd+Dijkstra hybrid, METIS partitioning, and distributed-GPU framework match the spec verbatim. Hardest call on gpu_single_card: the paper's core novelty is resolving a GPU-count-vs-block-count mismatch, i.e. it is designed around multi-GPU scaling (headline result: 2048 GPUs), though a single-GPU/single-partition degenerate case likely runs.

dynamic-graph-kernel|conf/ppopp/Hou0H00Y.regime: one-shot streaming temporal motif counting over complete historical temporal-edge logs (wikitalk/stackoverflow/temporal-reddit-reply/ethereum), chunked cache-regularized execution, CPU
dynamic-graph-kernel|conf/ppopp/Hou0H00Y.rationale: DTMiner's own real temporal-graph suite and evaluation shape are the literal basis for the spec's dgk-temporal-batch-throughput variant; headline is the Load-Explore-Synchronize execution model for exactly this kernel.

eigensolver|conf/ppopp/WangDZWZLJZ25.regime: dense symmetric tridiagonalization on GPU, fp64
eigensolver|conf/ppopp/WangDZWZLJZ25.rationale: cuEV's headline IS a GPU tridiagonalization algorithm (double-blocking band reduction + bulge chasing), explicitly named as the tridiagonalization-stage basis for the dense full-spectrum EVD variant, beating cuSOLVER/MAGMA.

eigensolver|conf/ppopp/YangNYLDXJ026.regime: sparse matrix-power kernel (MPK) for polynomial preconditioners, applied to both linear AND eigenvalue solves, CPU/Arm
eigensolver|conf/ppopp/YangNYLDXJ026.rationale: DBMPK optimizes the general matrix-power kernel used by polynomial preconditioners for both linear systems and eigenproblems; it is not itself an eigensolver implementation, so it is a real but separable component of the Krylov-filtered partial-spectrum pipeline. CPU/Arm only.

eigensolver|conf/sc/WangHZSJWDZ25.regime: 2-stage dense symmetric EVD back-transformation on GPU, fp64
eigensolver|conf/sc/WangHZSJWDZ25.rationale: This paper's headline IS a restructured EVD back-transformation algorithm, explicitly named as the back-transformation-stage basis for the dense full-spectrum EVD variant, beating MAGMA/cuSOLVER by up to 3.58x/2.21x.

eigensolver|journals/tpds/LiaoLLR21.regime: distributed structured divide-and-conquer symmetric tridiagonal eigensolver, fp64
eigensolver|journals/tpds/LiaoLLR21.rationale: PSDC is explicitly named as 'the one distributed paper in this track' and the exact basis for the eigensolver-symmetric-tridiagonal-dc-distributed variant (its own Clement/Hermite/Toeplitz generators and strong-scaling sizes). CPU/distributed only.

eigensolver|journals/tpds/ShiLXSH21.regime: polynomial-filtered partial-spectrum eigensolver, planetary normal-mode FEM operators, fp64
eigensolver|journals/tpds/ShiLXSH21.rationale: This paper's own four shipped FEM models are the explicit, verbatim basis for the polynomial-filtered partial-spectrum variant's tier (a). Distributed CPU, no GPU.

embedding-ops|conf/ics/RandallA021.regime: Word2Vec single-index embedding gather plus fused elementwise update with data-reuse optimization, single NVIDIA GPU (P100/V100)
embedding-ops|conf/ics/RandallA021.rationale: The spec's embed-single-index-gather variant explicitly names this paper's style ('KGE and word-embedding workloads (cuKE, FULL-W2V style)') as its defining shape.

embedding-ops|conf/ipps/HuLJ24.regime: KGE score-function fused tensor ops (TransE/TransH/TransR/TransF/RESCAL family), single NVIDIA GPU
embedding-ops|conf/ipps/HuLJ24.rationale: cuKE's own evaluated score functions are exactly the spec's embed-single-index-gather recommended_subset; headline is a code generator fusing these score-function tensor ops.

embedding-ops|conf/sc/PanZZXWSLR0D24.regime: fused per-field embedding-operator kernels for DLRM-style recsys at MLPerf/EL-Rec-scale table configs, single NVIDIA GPU
embedding-ops|conf/sc/PanZZXWSLR0D24.rationale: RecFlex's own table configs and end-to-end sampling convention (sample_batch_nums default) are named directly as the basis for the spec's embed-dlrm-pooled-kernel-f32 and embed-dlrm-e2e-preproc variants.

embedding-ops|conf/sc/WangWFMMD22.regime: Tensor-Train (TT) factorized/compressed embedding-table lookup for DLRM training, single GPU
embedding-ops|conf/sc/WangWFMMD22.rationale: EL-Rec's headline contribution is a TT-decomposed compressed embedding table (a structurally different, factorized representation reconstructed via small tensor contractions), not the plain dense/uncompressed table gather+pool or single-index lookup either named variant assumes.

erasure-coding|conf/sc/Uezato21.regime: CPU XOR-based Reed-Solomon, (k,m) configurations, three-tier optimization ablation
erasure-coding|conf/sc/Uezato21.rationale: The spec's ec-xor-encode-decode-kernel variant is built directly around this paper's own (k,m) configurations and Nooptim/Fusion/FusionSchedule ablation. CPU single-thread, no GPU.

fft|conf/ipps/ChengSWB26.regime: ring-FFT-plus-Legendre-transform embedded in a differentiable spherical-harmonic-transform library on HEALPix grids
fft|conf/ipps/ChengSWB26.rationale: FFT is one computational stage of cuHPX's SHT pipeline, not the paper's headline; explicitly named in the spec (cuHPX's 3*nside-1 length) for the batched-kernel variant selection.

fft|conf/ipps/RenUDKLYCG26.regime: FFT embedded in a GPU spectral error-correction pass atop lossy compressors, cosmology/X-ray/combustion grids
fft|conf/ipps/RenUDKLYCG26.rationale: FFT is a computational sub-step of FFCz's compression-correction pipeline, not the headline; explicitly named in the spec's fft-ndgrid-e2e variant with FFCz's own README grid size (512^3).

fft|conf/ppopp/HanLCBZYCZCY25.regime: FFT-based technique bridging to dense stencil computation on Tensor Core Units, lengths 56/64/128
fft|conf/ppopp/HanLCBZYCZCY25.rationale: The headline result is stencil-computation speedup achieved via an FFT-based reformulation on tensor cores, not FFT throughput itself; explicitly named in the spec's fft-1d-batched-kernel selection.

fft|conf/ppopp/WuZ0HJDDCC25.regime: power-of-two 1D C2C FFT, fp32/fp64, NVIDIA GPU, directly vs cuFFT/VkFFT
fft|conf/ppopp/WuZ0HJDDCC25.rationale: TurboFFT's headline IS a GPU FFT kernel evaluated at kernel level against cuFFT/VkFFT; the spec's fft-1d-batched-kernel variant is built directly around its own N=2^9..2^25 sweep.

fft|conf/sc/BrunnHBMM20.regime: FFT as one of several kernels (interpolation, finite-difference, FFT) in a multi-GPU image-registration Gauss-Newton-Krylov solver, single-V100 and 256-GPU scale points
fft|conf/sc/BrunnHBMM20.rationale: FFT is one of several named computational kernels inside CLAIRE's larger registration-solver pipeline, not the headline; explicitly named in the spec's fft-distributed-alltoall and fft-ndgrid-e2e variants with its own 256^3/49,152-core/256-GPU scale points.

fft|conf/sc/WuZDZHC25.regime: fused FFT-GEMM-iFFT for Fourier Neural Operators, N in {64,128}, NVIDIA GPU; FFT built from scratch and compared to cuFFT
fft|conf/sc/WuZDZHC25.rationale: TurboFNO builds and benchmarks its own FFT kernel against cuFFT (grouped with TurboFFT as a track denominator), but its N range ({64,128}) is far narrower than TurboFFT's full sweep and the FFT is fused with GEMM rather than measured standalone.

fft|journals/tpds/BaltyCG23.regime: distributed 3D FFT, weak scaling to 49,152 CPU cores via MPI all-to-all
fft|journals/tpds/BaltyCG23.rationale: FLUPS's headline IS a distributed FFT library; explicitly one of only two track papers the spec's fft-distributed-alltoall variant is built around. CPU+MPI only, no GPU.

fft|journals/tpds/LiWSYDZ26.regime: memory-efficient FFT used for polynomial multiplication inside a GPU post-quantum signature scheme, N in {512,1024}
fft|journals/tpds/LiWSYDZ26.rationale: FFT is an internal building block of the Falcon signing pipeline, not the headline contribution; explicitly named in the spec's fft-1d-batched-kernel variant selection (Falcon_N in {512,1024}).

fft|journals/tpds/ZhangLW20.regime: batched small-tensor tubal-sampling completion on synthetic data; FFT used only as an algorithmic convolution-theorem trick, never separately benchmarked
fft|journals/tpds/ZhangLW20.rationale: FFT is merely invoked as a mathematical device to decouple the completion problem into per-frequency subproblems; no FFT-specific kernel optimization or standalone throughput number is reported.

fft|journals/tpds/ZhangLWW20.regime: t-FFT as one of 7 tensor primitives (t-product/t-SVD/t-QR/t-inverse are the headline speedup numbers) for small tubal-rank tensors, based/streamed/batched execution modes
fft|journals/tpds/ZhangLWW20.rationale: t-FFT is one of seven named GPU primitives in a broader tensor-operations library; survey.md flags this as only lightly surveyed with no t-FFT-specific timing/precision/baseline recoverable, and the batched small-tensor regime doesn't match either the 1D-sweep or grid-E2E variants.

gemm|conf/asplos/DingYZLWP23.regime: DL tensor-program GEMM/conv2d shapes on NVIDIA GPUs via task-mapping compiler
gemm|conf/asplos/DingYZLWP23.rationale: Hidet is a compiler paradigm producing fast GPU kernels for DL tensor programs (GEMM and conv2d among them); GEMM is one of the operator types it targets, not the sole headline kernel.

gemm|conf/asplos/IkarashiQDRBR25.regime: 80+ hand-schedulable HPC/DL kernels including GEMM, cross-platform (CPU/ARM)
gemm|conf/asplos/IkarashiQDRBR25.rationale: Exo 2 is a user-extensible scheduling-language compiler whose evaluation spans 80+ kernels including GEMM; matches the 'autotuner/DSL that generates this kernel among others' component pattern. CPU/ARM only, exact shape overlap with the track's sweep unconfirmed.

gemm|conf/asplos/YuLZCFX24.regime: dynamic-shape DL tensor-program GEMM on GPU Tensor Cores / Ascend NPU
gemm|conf/asplos/YuLZCFX24.rationale: MikPoly is a dynamic-shape tensor compiler (micro-kernel polymerization) evaluated across GEMM and other dynamic-shape operators vs. vendor libraries; GEMM is one of several operator types it targets, and shapes are dynamic-DL-derived rather than the fixed sweep.

gemm|conf/cgo/LopezKB26.regime: symbolic-size BLAS/LAPACK kernel-chain sequencing overhead, not a standalone GEMM benchmark
gemm|conf/cgo/LopezKB26.rationale: Headline is a multi-versioning codegen that selects/sequences BLAS/LAPACK kernel calls (GEMM among TRSM/SYRK/etc.) for symbolic-size chains; the reported metric is FLOPs/time within 15% of optimal chain cost, not GEMM throughput vs. a vendor baseline. CPU only.

gemm|conf/cgo/LopoukhineFVLDD25.regime: RISC-V streaming-register-accelerator DNN micro-kernels, FPU-utilization metric, not GEMM GFLOP/s
gemm|conf/cgo/LopoukhineFVLDD25.rationale: An MLIR compiler backend that generates generic 'DNN micro-kernels' (GEMM-like) for a custom RISC-V accelerator; evaluated via FPU utilization %, not vendor-comparable GEMM throughput. Platform is a custom accelerator, not CPU/GPU/FPGA in the track's sense.

gemm|conf/cgo/ZhangDSHSP26.regime: DL-shaped (attention/MoE-adjacent) fp16 tensor-core GEMM via an auto-layout-synthesis compiler
gemm|conf/cgo/ZhangDSHSP26.rationale: Hexcute is a layout-synthesis compiler that generates many kernel types (GEMM, FlashAttention, MoE); it reports matching cuBLAS on GEMM but the shapes are DL-workload-derived rather than the track's square/irregular sweep.

gemm|conf/dac/AlshboulTS20.regime: matrix-multiply as case-study kernel for NVMM write-reduction tiling; no vendor-baseline throughput comparison
gemm|conf/dac/AlshboulTS20.rationale: WET studies the effect of loop tiling on NVMM write amplification using matrix multiplication as its case-study kernel; the metric is write-count reduction (and secondarily performance), not GEMM throughput vs. cuBLAS/MKL-class baselines. CPU only.

gemm|conf/dac/BasalamaWC23.rationale: Odyssey is a DSE tool that explores tiling/dataflow for systolic-array designs across 'various matrix multiplication and convolution kernels' -- an autotuner generating multiple kernel-family designs, not a dedicated GEMM implementation. FPGA only.

gemm|conf/dac/ZhuangYZ23.regime: Versal ACAP systolic-array matmul accelerator, FP32/INT16/INT8
gemm|conf/dac/ZhuangYZ23.rationale: AutoMM/CHARM is dedicated specifically to generating matrix-multiply accelerator designs (not a multi-kernel-family DSE tool), evaluated kernel-level (GFLOPs/TOPs) against A100/U250/TX2; but its INT16/INT8 emphasis and FPGA/ACAP target diverge from the spec's fp64/32/16 CPU/GPU-focused sweep.

gemm|conf/ics/DezfuliC25.regime: sparse-dependence-fused dense/SpMM matmul for GNN training and sparse solves
gemm|conf/ics/DezfuliC25.rationale: Tile-fusion is a compiler technique fusing a dense matmul loop with a sparse (SpMM) loop for GNN/solver pipelines; GEMM is one half of a fused kernel evaluated via GNN-training and sparse-solve speedups, not standalone dense GEMM throughput. CPU only.

gemm|conf/ics/LiXSS24.regime: TVM-tuned GEMM/2D-convolution shapes; the claim is auto-tuning search time, not raw GEMM throughput
gemm|conf/ics/LiXSS24.rationale: This is an autotuning-acceleration paper (faster TVM search for GEMM and conv2d kernels), matching the 'autotuner that generates this kernel among others' component pattern; the headline metric is tuning-time reduction, not kernel throughput vs. a fixed baseline.

gemm|conf/ics/WuZLHJWC23.regime: large/near-square dense GEMM, fp32/fp64, GPU, incl. irregular shapes
gemm|conf/ics/WuZLHJWC23.rationale: This paper's own 1024-6144-step-512 square sweep is explicitly the cited basis for the track's gemm-square-kernel variant; headline is a from-scratch GEMM kernel beating/matching cuBLAS.

gemm|conf/ics/ZhangSW20.regime: Tensor-Core low-rank Gram-matrix approximation (random-projection matmul) for SVM training
gemm|conf/ics/ZhangSW20.rationale: GEMM/matmul is used to compute a Tensor-Core-accelerated low-rank Gram-matrix approximation inside an SVM training system; it is a real, separable sub-kernel of a larger ML training pipeline, not independently GEMM-benchmarked.

gemm|conf/ipps/BellavitaRICDVG26.regime: distributed multi-GPU dense/sparse GEMM primitives tailored to Kernel K-means, not general-purpose square GEMM
gemm|conf/ipps/BellavitaRICDVG26.rationale: GEMM/SpGEMM appear only as communication-efficient primitives inside a distributed Kernel K-means clustering algorithm evaluated end-to-end (weak-scaling efficiency to 256 GPUs); no standalone GEMM benchmark, and the contribution is fundamentally multi-GPU distributed, not a single-card path.

gemm|conf/ipps/DengYFD26.regime: small/irregular DeepSeek/LLaMA-derived GEMM shapes, multi-precision, ARM SME
gemm|conf/ipps/DengYFD26.rationale: MPGEMM's headline IS an open-source GEMM library evaluated kernel-level against Apple Accelerate/OpenBLAS/Eigen; its DeepSeek/LLaMA shapes are explicitly one of the spec's own cited sources for the small-irregular variant. CPU (ARM) only, no GPU.

gemm|conf/ipps/GeorganasKVKNPB24.regime: CPU DL/HPC kernels (incl. GEMM) via Tensor Processing Primitives + declarative loops
gemm|conf/ipps/GeorganasKVKNPB24.rationale: TPP-MLIR is a broader framework producing portable near-peak DL/HPC kernels via TPPs and loop abstractions; GEMM is one of several kernel types generated, evaluated with standalone and end-to-end workloads. CPU only.

gemm|conf/ipps/LiYTLZ22.regime: DGEMM on AMD GPU via Tensile auto-tuning, batched and single
gemm|conf/ipps/LiYTLZ22.rationale: Tensile-FGPS's headline is a fine-grained prefetching scheme for DGEMM kernels, evaluated kernel-level and explicitly named in the spec text; but the GPU is AMD, not NVIDIA, so out of the benchmark's single-NVIDIA-GPU scope.

gemm|conf/ipps/YaoZLX26.regime: Ozaki-scheme FP16 tensor-core convolution-reformulated stencil update, not a standalone dense GEMM
gemm|conf/ipps/YaoZLX26.rationale: GEMM here is a reformulation vehicle for a shallow-water stencil dynamical core (headline is the PDE solver); there is no standalone dense-GEMM kernel benchmark against vendor libraries.

gemm|conf/ppopp/ChenLWBWMYZCY24.regime: stencil-to-matmul transformation on Tensor Cores, not a general dense GEMM benchmark
gemm|conf/ppopp/ChenLWBWMYZCY24.rationale: ConvStencil transforms stencil computation into matmul to exploit Tensor Cores; headline and baselines are stencil-domain (speedup over stencil solvers), not GEMM vs. vendor libraries.

gemm|conf/ppopp/JangdaY24.regime: Kronecker-structured matrix-matrix multiplication, a distinct operation from general dense GEMM
gemm|conf/ppopp/JangdaY24.rationale: FastKron implements Kronecker-product matrix multiplication (multiplication with a Kronecker product of several smaller matrices), a structurally different operation from the spec's C=A*B GEMM; baselines are tensor-algebra libraries, not cuBLAS-style GEMM.

gemm|conf/ppopp/XuSZLH024.regime: PolyBench affine-kernel suite (GEMM one of ~30 kernels) under mixed-precision autotuning
gemm|conf/ppopp/XuSZLH024.rationale: PrecTuner is a general mixed-precision code generator/autotuner for PolyBench affine programs; GEMM is a generic example among many affine kernels, not a dedicated GEMM optimization target.

gemm|conf/sc/FuXGMSWSD0Y25.regime: tensor-core cross-correlation difference kernel for cryo-EM, not a general dense GEMM
gemm|conf/sc/FuXGMSWSD0Y25.rationale: The accelerated kernel is a cryo-EM cross-correlation/difference computation reformulated via Tensor Cores, not a general-purpose GEMM; evaluated against RELION's own baseline, not vendor GEMM libraries.

gemm|conf/sc/HuangC22.regime: distributed dense matrix multiplication, arbitrary M=N=K, fp64
gemm|conf/sc/HuangC22.rationale: CA3DMM is explicitly the named source algorithm for the gemm-distributed-e2e variant (same example sizing rationale, ntest=10 convention); CPU-only distributed, no GPU.

gemm|conf/sc/LiuLLFYSZWPCGHW21.regime: tensor-contraction-based quantum-circuit simulation on Sunway many-core, not standalone dense GEMM
gemm|conf/sc/LiuLLFYSZWPCGHW21.rationale: GEMM/matmul appears as a fused permute-multiply primitive deep inside a 42-million-core tensor-network quantum-circuit simulator; evaluated via whole-application EFLOPS, not a GEMM benchmark. Sunway platform, no NVIDIA GPU.

gemm|conf/sc/LtaiefACRSKDBAK24.regime: GWAS/KRR-specific mixed-precision GEMM inside a tile Cholesky-based solver, application-sized matrices
gemm|conf/sc/LtaiefACRSKDBAK24.rationale: GEMM is a real, separable BLAS3 building block used inside the paper's tile-Cholesky-based KRR solver for GWAS; it is not independently benchmarked against vendor GEMM at the track's square/irregular sizes.

gemm|conf/sc/MatteisLH20.regime: streaming HLS BLAS3 GEMM (and other BLAS routines) on FPGA
gemm|conf/sc/MatteisLH20.rationale: fBLAS is an open-source BLAS library whose evaluated routines include GEMM as a primary BLAS3 member; but its streaming, on-chip-communication-composed design differs from the spec's off-chip square/irregular DRAM-resident sweep. FPGA only.

gemm|conf/sc/WangHZSJWDZ25.regime: one incidental GEMM call inside an EVD back-transformation reordering, not a benchmarked GEMM kernel
gemm|conf/sc/WangHZSJWDZ25.rationale: GEMM appears only as 'one additional GEMM computation' incurred by restructuring EVD back-transformation; the paper's kernel and baselines are all EVD-specific (MAGMA/cuSOLVER), not a GEMM benchmark.

gemm|conf/sc/WuMZDW0WW24.regime: small/irregular (tall-skinny, long-rectangular) GEMM on Arm CPUs
gemm|conf/sc/WuMZDW0WW24.rationale: autoGEMM's headline IS an autotuned irregular-GEMM micro-kernel generator, evaluated kernel-level against LIBXSMM/LibShalom/OpenBLAS/Eigen; explicitly one of the cited source artifacts for the small-irregular variant. Arm CPU only.

gemm|conf/sc/WuZDZHC25.regime: fp32/fp16 GEMM sized to Fourier Neural Operator hidden dimensions, fused with FFT/iFFT
gemm|conf/sc/WuZDZHC25.rationale: TurboFNO builds a real from-scratch GEMM kernel matching/exceeding cuBLAS, but the headline contribution is the fused FFT-GEMM-iFFT operator for FNOs; GEMM is one stage of that fused pipeline, sized to FNO workloads rather than the track's independent square/irregular sweep.

gemm|conf/sc/YangFDSW21.rationale: LibShalom's headline IS an optimized small/irregular GEMM library, explicitly and repeatedly cited as a canonical source for the gemm-small-irregular-kernel variant. Arm CPU only.

gemm|conf/sc/ZhangLYCZCY24.regime: low-rank stencil-weight decomposition on Tensor Cores, not a general dense GEMM
gemm|conf/sc/ZhangLYCZCY24.rationale: LoRAStencil decomposes stencil weight matrices into rank-1 factors to reduce TCU memory-access redundancy for stencil computation; it is not a GEMM implementation or benchmark.

gemm|journals/tpds/LanMHSDWLQF20.regime: Winograd-transform tile GEMM (TensorGEMM) embedded in CNN inference, ARM CPU
gemm|journals/tpds/LanMHSDWLQF20.rationale: TensorGEMM accelerates Winograd-transformed convolution tiles inside the FeatherCNN inference library; GEMM performance is reported but the shapes are small Winograd-tile-specific, not the general square/irregular sweep, and the headline is the CNN inference framework. ARM CPU only.

gemm|journals/tpds/LichtBMH21.regime: GEMM as one illustrative HLS-transformation case study, not a dedicated optimized GEMM implementation
gemm|journals/tpds/LichtBMH21.rationale: This is a catalog/tutorial of HLS optimizing transformations demonstrated on a sample set of HPC kernels (GEMM, stencil); GEMM is an example, not a competitively-optimized, vendor-baseline-compared implementation.

gemm|journals/tpds/LinXWYLL25.regime: OpenCL GEMM on FPGA/OpenCL devices, square + GEMMBATCHED sweeps
gemm|journals/tpds/LinXWYLL25.rationale: CL-DB-GEMM's headline IS an optimized, Bayesian-autotuned OpenCL GEMM kernel; its own 'multiples of 128/129' square sweep and GEMMBATCHED/GEMMSTRIDEDBATCHED sweep are literally the cited basis for this track's square and batched variants. FPGA/OpenCL, no NVIDIA GPU.

gemm|journals/tpds/NavarroQMFH25.regime: cellular-automata neighborhood update reformulated as tensor-core matmul, not benchmarked as GEMM
gemm|journals/tpds/NavarroQMFH25.rationale: CAT maps a CA transition function onto tensor-core matmul; results are reported in CA-domain metrics (speedup vs. GPU/CPU CA baselines) not GEMM GFLOP/s against vendor libraries.

gemv|conf/asplos/LamJ0MGLLLRLRW024.regime: compute-bound LWE-ring modular-arithmetic matrix-vector multiply for private information retrieval
gemv|conf/asplos/LamJ0MGLLLRLRW024.rationale: GPU-DPF's MVM kernel is real and separable but embedded in a larger PIR system (evaluated via end-to-end QPS and PIR-ML co-design gains); the spec itself flags this kernel as compute- not memory-bound, unlike the memory-bandwidth-bound regime this track targets.

gemv|conf/cgo/PegolottiAP26.regime: nonuniform-bitwidth (INT2/3/4) quantized-weight GEMV, CPU, LLM linear layers
gemv|conf/cgo/PegolottiAP26.rationale: QIGen's headline IS a kernel generator producing nonuniformly-quantized matrix-vector kernels for LLM inference; explicitly the named source for the gemv-quantized-weight-kernel variant. CPU only.

gemv|conf/ipps/JiangYLHDJ26.regime: KV-cache-compressed GEMV on NVIDIA GPUs, LLM decode
gemv|conf/ipps/JiangYLHDJ26.rationale: This is the instructions' own worked example: PackKV's headline is KV-cache lossy compression; GEMV acceleration is an additional benefit of the compression scheme, matching the gemv-e2e-compressed-format variant it is cited for.

gemv|conf/ppopp/FrantarCCHA25.regime: INT4-quantized-weight GEMV/GEMM batch sweep crossing the memory/compute-bound roofline knee, GPU, LLM linear layers
gemv|conf/ppopp/FrantarCCHA25.rationale: MARLIN's headline IS mixed-precision GPU GEMM/GEMV kernels for LLM inference; its bench.py MODELS dict and full batch-size ALL=True sweep are the explicit, verbatim basis for the gemv-quantized-weight-kernel and gemv-batched-decode variants.

gemv|conf/sc/LtaiefHWJRK23.regime: tile low-rank matrix-vector multiply, seismic MDD real datasets, Cerebras CS-2
gemv|conf/sc/LtaiefHWJRK23.rationale: TLR-MVM is explicitly the named source for the gemv-e2e-compressed-format variant (same seismic-redatuming datasets, same bench.cpp harness). Platform is Cerebras CS-2, not an NVIDIA GPU.

gnn-aggregation|conf/asplos/PengXSHZHKKD.regime: MaxK top-k-sparsified (CBSR-format) SpGEMM/SSpMM aggregation kernel, single A100, custom 24-graph kernel benchmark plus a 5-dataset full training pipeline
gnn-aggregation|conf/asplos/PengXSHZHKKD.rationale: Headline is a fast GPU SpMM/SSpMM kernel design reducing GNN memory traffic, with an isolated kernel-level benchmark harness (kernels/spmm_base.h) shared with cuSPARSE/GNNAdvisor baselines; but the actual operand is a structurally top-k-sparsified feature matrix, not the plain dense-N-column input the kernel-f32 variant specifies.

gnn-aggregation|conf/hpdc/FuJH22.regime: isolated kernel-only GNN aggregation call (vertex+feature two-level parallelism), dataset-agnostic real-graph CSR (citeseer worked example), N=32 default, single V100
gnn-aggregation|conf/hpdc/FuJH22.rationale: TLPGNN's own benchmark (gcn/test_kernel.py) is the narrowest, purest kernel-only scope surveyed in this track -- exactly the spec's kernel-f32 variant's claim.

gnn-aggregation|conf/ics/0001SLFY024.regime: segmented/batched dense GEMM per relation-type for heterogeneous GNNs (RGCN/HGT/RGAT), H100/A100/RTX4090
gnn-aggregation|conf/ics/0001SLFY024.rationale: FASTEN's operator is segmented (grouped/batched) dense GEMM over relational graph types, not the sparse-adjacency-times-dense-feature aggregation this track's spec defines; its own categories tag it dense_la, not sparse_la, and the assignment to gnn-aggregation looks like a mismatch on operator identity.

gnn-aggregation|conf/ipps/AlvesMBFGR25.regime: binary-adjacency x dense-feature matmul (plain and degree-normalized GCN aggregation), CPU shared-memory (serial+parallel), SNAP/Planetoid/OGB graphs overlapping the recommended subset (Cora, PubMed),
gnn-aggregation|conf/ipps/AlvesMBFGR25.rationale: Headline is the CBM compression format specifically for accelerating binary@dense aggregation matmul; kernel-only timing (benchmark_matmul.py) is cleanly separated from format-conversion cost, matching the spec's kernel-f32 variant closely.

gnn-aggregation|conf/ppopp/WangFD22.regime: quantized (1/2/4/8-bit) bit-decomposed Tensor-Core GNN aggregation, plus a separate synthetic INT8 GEMM comparison untethered to any real graph, Ampere-class GPU
gnn-aggregation|conf/ppopp/WangFD22.rationale: QGTC's headline contribution is a Tensor-Core kernel design for quantized GNN aggregation, but its precision axis (1-8-bit bit-decomposed) is not commensurable with the spec's fp32 dense-feature variant, which has no quantized counterpart in this track.

gnn-aggregation|conf/sc/HeLDL0M025.regime: full GCN training via a GPU Strassen's-algorithm SpMM, single GPU (RTX 4090); no isolated kernel-level benchmark exposed and exact dataset names not confirmed from the README
gnn-aggregation|conf/sc/HeLDL0M025.rationale: Headline is 'the first GPU-accelerated SpMM implementation based on Strassen's algorithm' for GCN training -- centrally about the aggregation kernel -- but the public artifact only exposes full-training numbers (matches the epoch-training-e2e variant's tier), and the dataset suite could not be independently confirmed.

gnn-aggregation|conf/sc/HuYWYZL0ZW20.regime: co-optimized sparse-template+UDF GNN aggregation kernel via TVM autotuning, dataset-agnostic CSR input (Reddit worked example), feature width 128, CPU and GPU dual backend
gnn-aggregation|conf/sc/HuYWYZL0ZW20.rationale: FeatGraph's whole contribution is optimizing the SpMM-like GNN aggregation operator via composable sparse templates and UDFs; it is dataset-agnostic like the spec's suite and reports both CPU and single-GPU kernel-level speedups.

gnn-aggregation|conf/sc/HuangD0Y20.regime: isolated kernel-only GNN SpMM, SNAP/SuiteSparse graphs (whole SNAP category mirrored), N in {128,256,512}, fp32, single GPU
gnn-aggregation|conf/sc/HuangD0Y20.rationale: GE-SpMM is explicitly named as one of the papers defining the kernel-f32 variant's 'common denominator', and its dataset-sweep convention (N doubling 128->256->512) is reused verbatim by the spec.

gnn-aggregation|conf/sc/TripathyYB20.regime: distributed multi-GPU 1D/1.5D/2D/3D parallel decomposition of GNN aggregation; local SpMM uses whichever library is available and is not itself optimized, torch.distributed on 100+ GPUs
gnn-aggregation|conf/sc/TripathyYB20.rationale: CAGNET's contribution and measured quantity is communication volume/time for a family of parallel decompositions, not local kernel throughput -- the aggregation kernel is used as an unoptimized sub-step (per survey.md), and the paper's target scenario is inherently multi-GPU-only.

gnn-aggregation|conf/usenix/WangFWHD23.regime: isolated single-kernel SpMM/SDDMM plus full-epoch GCN training on GNNAdvisor-lineage real graphs heavily overlapping the recommended subset (citeseer/cora/pubmed/ppi/amazon0505/artist/soc-BlogCatalog/
gnn-aggregation|conf/usenix/WangFWHD23.rationale: TC-GNN is one of the few papers in this track that ships both an isolated kernel-only benchmark AND an epoch-level model benchmark, and its 14-graph suite overlaps heavily with the spec's recommended_subset for both the kernel-f32 and epoch-training-e2e variants.

gnn-aggregation|journals/tpds/XuSYLJ22.regime: GCN backward aggregation restructured as a partial-active-vertex GPU kernel, both kernel-only (1.48-5.65x) and with/without-preprocessing end-to-end numbers, real GNNAdvisor-lineage graphs, GPU
gnn-aggregation|journals/tpds/XuSYLJ22.rationale: EPPGCN is the paper the spec's preprocessing-amortized e2e variant is explicitly modeled on -- it is the only surveyed paper reporting both a with- and without-preprocessing end-to-end number side by side alongside a kernel-only figure.

graph-layout|conf/sc/LiSDHGGPGZ24.regime: GPU-accelerated 2D force-directed / PG-SGD layout of pangenome variation graphs, complete HPRC Year-1 whole-chromosome suite (24 graphs), single NVIDIA GPU
graph-layout|conf/sc/LiSDHGGPGZ24.rationale: This is the sole surveyed paper and exact match for the spec's suite (evaluated on all 24 human whole-chromosome pangenomes, precisely the recommended_subset's source); headline is the GPU pangenome-layout kernel itself.

graph-partitioning|conf/dac/LeeLHJHL024.regime: DIMACS10-scale graphs, small power-of-2 k, GPU
graph-partitioning|conf/dac/LeeLHJHL024.rationale: G-kway's own operating point directly defines the spec's gp-kernel-small-k variant.

graph-partitioning|conf/ipps/SalwasserSG.regime: trillion-edge web/synthetic graphs, large k, CPU/distributed
graph-partitioning|conf/ipps/SalwasserSG.rationale: TeraPart's own operating point and headline 16x peak-memory reduction directly define the spec's gp-kernel-large-k and gp-memory-scaling variants.

graph-pattern-mining|conf/asplos/XieZLCJ.regime: variable-length graph pattern matching (path queries of unbounded/variable length) on billion-edge graphs
graph-pattern-mining|conf/asplos/XieZLCJ.rationale: The spec explicitly excludes VertexSurge from all variants because it measures variable-length path queries, not counting occurrences of a FIXED-shape pattern, which the spec calls a different operation that would misrepresent the comparison if forced in.

graph-pattern-mining|conf/ppopp/CaoMLT25.regime: clique-ladder (K4-K7) and pattern counting on SNAP-style graphs (mico/patents/youtube/pokec) via LUT connectivity checks
graph-pattern-mining|conf/ppopp/CaoMLT25.rationale: GLumin is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers this spec's clique_ladder pattern set and small/large-pattern variants are built around (CliqueSolver k=4-7 explicitly named).

graph-pattern-mining|conf/ppopp/Hou0H00Y.regime: temporal motif mining with time-window queries on temporal graphs, not fixed-pattern counting on a static graph
graph-pattern-mining|conf/ppopp/Hou0H00Y.rationale: The spec explicitly excludes DTMiner from all variants, stating it measures a different operation entirely (temporal, time-window motif queries, not counting occurrences of a fixed pattern in a static graph) — an assignment the spec itself flags as not fitting this track.

graph-pattern-mining|conf/ppopp/LinMSZXT.regime: set-centric GPM with redundancy elimination, clique-ladder + 4-motif census (G2Miner gallery) on 11 graphs
graph-pattern-mining|conf/ppopp/LinMSZXT.rationale: GraphFold is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers and its TC/CF4-7/MC4/P1-8 pattern gallery is directly incorporated into the spec's pattern_set and recommended_subset.

graph-pattern-mining|conf/ppopp/ParkOK24.regime: large-output triangle LISTING (not counting) via chunked kernel restart on RMAT/real graphs
graph-pattern-mining|conf/ppopp/ParkOK24.rationale: INFINEL's search kernel is closely related (triangle enumeration) but the spec's own notes_on_fairness explicitly calls listing 'architecturally different' from the counting operation its core variants measure (IO-bound on materialized output vs a pure count) and excludes it from the core counting variants.

graph-pattern-mining|conf/sc/BradleyAB25.regime: GPU subgraph counting with fringe-vertex pruning on named real+synthetic graphs, edges/s throughput
graph-pattern-mining|conf/sc/BradleyAB25.rationale: Fringe-SGC is the sole surveyed paper reporting a throughput metric and is the direct source of the spec's GEPS (edges-processed-per-second) metric convention.

graph-pattern-mining|conf/sc/JiangZJLZLC.regime: view-based multi-GPU subgraph matching, 19 named patterns + k-clique/k-motif sweeps on com-friendster
graph-pattern-mining|conf/sc/JiangZJLZLC.rationale: VSGM is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers and is literally cited by name for both the named_5v_plus pattern definitions and the com-friendster billion-edge graph in the spec's recommended_subset; its headline design is an explicit communication-hiding multi-GPU pipeline, so no meaningful single-GPU path is claimed.

graph-pattern-mining|conf/sc/ShiZWCZHYC2.regime: equivalent-set-transformation compiler for subgraph pattern counting, mico/patents/orkut/livejournal/friendster
graph-pattern-mining|conf/sc/ShiZWCZHYC2.rationale: GraphSet is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers and the only one with a real automated correctness oracle (gtest hardcoded references), which the spec adopts as its own correctness cross-check.

graph-pattern-mining|conf/sc/WeiJ22.regime: stack-based GPU pattern matching, 24 patterns (5-7 vertices) on wiki-Vote/Enron/youtube/LiveJournal
graph-pattern-mining|conf/sc/WeiJ22.rationale: STMatch is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers directly cited in the spec's recommended_subset (mico/cit-Patents/com-youtube usage) and pattern-size framing.

graph-pattern-mining|conf/sc/XiangKSHS21.regime: trie-based distributed multi-GPU subgraph isomorphism, 33 patterns on 6 SNAP graphs, cross-diffed vs GSI
graph-pattern-mining|conf/sc/XiangKSHS21.rationale: cuTS is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers whose 6 SNAP graphs and 33-pattern sweep the spec's suite selection draws on, but it is explicitly a distributed multi-GPU system, not a single-GPU candidate.

hamiltonian-simulation|conf/ics/Chundury.regime: diagonal-budgeted Trotterized Hamiltonian time evolution, HamLib suite, CPU+GPU
hamiltonian-simulation|conf/ics/Chundury.rationale: HamSim's headline IS the diagonal-budgeted Trotterization algorithm and diagonal-sparse SpMV kernel, the sole and direct basis for both variants (same HamLib families, same diagonal-density framing).

hash-table|conf/ipps/NisaPEOBY21.regime: 6 named real genomic k-mer datasets at k=17, GPU counting/upsert hash table embedded in a distributed communication-optimized pipeline
hash-table|conf/ipps/NisaPEOBY21.rationale: DEDUKT's paper-level speedups conflate hash-table counting with distributed communication/partitioning (which the spec's variant explicitly isolates out); it is the exact anchor for the spec's dataset list.

hash-table|conf/usenix/ChenHDZ20.regime: YCSB workloads, Zipfian(0.99)/uniform, 15-byte keys/values, lock-free concurrent hash table on Optane persistent memory
hash-table|conf/usenix/ChenHDZ20.rationale: Headline IS the concurrent hash-table design; explicitly the sole track anchor for the spec's CRUD-mixed-ops variant. CPU/PM only, no GPU.

hash-table|conf/usenix/ShovonGMK23.regime: 18 named real-world SNAP/DIMACS/road-network relations, GPU open-addressing build/probe join table, load_factor=0.4 fixed
hash-table|conf/usenix/ShovonGMK23.rationale: Survey.md states the paper's contribution is an iterative-Datalog transitive-closure engine using 'a standard equi-join build/probe table' as a supporting kernel, evaluated end-to-end via transitive closure rather than isolated hash-table throughput; its real relations are the explicit anchor for the spec's hash-table-build-probe-kernel variant.

hausdorff-distance|conf/ics/GengYLWZ26.regime: medical/geospatial/3D-graphics point sets, RT-core+CUDA Hausdorff distance vs ITK/brute-force
hausdorff-distance|conf/ics/GengYLWZ26.rationale: The entire track spec is built directly around X-HD's own CLI, algorithm variants, and dataset domains.

homotopy-continuation|conf/ipps/ChienAK2.regime: GPU homotopy-continuation path tracking (fixed-work + RANSAC-gated) for trifocal pose estimation, single GPU
homotopy-continuation|conf/ipps/ChienAK2.rationale: This is the sole surveyed paper and the entire basis for this track's spec, with every problem constant (Num_Of_Vars, Num_Of_Tracks, GPUHC_Max_Steps, etc.) read verbatim from its own artifact config.

json-parsing|conf/asplos/GargaryL026.regime: fully GPU-offloaded JSON parsing (UTF-8 validate+tokenize+nest), standard corpora
json-parsing|conf/asplos/GargaryL026.rationale: cuJSON's headline IS a GPU JSON-parsing algorithm/kernel, the sole and direct basis for this track's only variant.

kcore-kclique|conf/ics/AlmasriHNXH22.regime: exact k-clique counting on GPU, SNAP graphs
kcore-kclique|conf/ics/AlmasriHNXH22.rationale: KCGPU's headline IS a parallel GPU k-clique-counting kernel, explicitly the basis for the kclique-count-exact variant (its own Table 1 graph set).

kcore-kclique|conf/ppopp/LiuSZ24.regime: batch-dynamic k-core maintenance under streamed edge updates, CPU
kcore-kclique|conf/ppopp/LiuSZ24.rationale: LiuSZ24's headline IS a parallel batch-dynamic k-core decomposition data structure, explicitly and repeatedly named as the source for the kcore-dynamic-batch variant (its own dynamic graph streams and batch sizes). CPU only.

kcore-kclique|conf/ppopp/PanQZ26.regime: maximal clique enumeration on large real graphs (up to 146B cliques), GPU
kcore-kclique|conf/ppopp/PanQZ26.rationale: RDMCE's headline IS a GPU MCE algorithm/kernel, explicitly and by name the basis for the mce-enum variant, including its own SNAP/nrvis/KONECT graph suite.

kcore-kclique|conf/ppopp/Shun20.regime: hypergraph (bipartite vertex-hyperedge) algorithms, k-core one of ~8 algorithms covered
kcore-kclique|conf/ppopp/Shun20.rationale: The spec itself explicitly excludes this paper's hypergraph inputs as a structurally different data model (bipartite incidence, not a plain adjacency list); k-core is only one of eight algorithms (betweenness, PageRank, SSSP, etc.) in a general hypergraph-processing framework, not a dedicated k-core/k-clique contribution.

kcore-kclique|conf/sc/BestaMLTIKAJPKGVMH.rationale: ProbGraph's headline IS Bloom-filter probabilistic set representations applied to clique counting and clustering, explicitly the basis for the kclique-count-approx variant (its own Table VIII graph suite). CPU only.

knn-graph-construction|conf/ipps/Ranawak.regime: high-dimensional ANN-benchmark-style point sets, distributed CPU
knn-graph-construction|conf/ipps/Ranawak.rationale: This is the sole paper the knn-graph-construction spec was built around; its distributed sparse random-projection-tree algorithm and MPI-process scaling directly define both spec variants. No GPU in the artifact.

lca-bridge-finding|conf/ipps/0001SS21.regime: GPU Euler-tour LCA batch queries and bridge-finding on synthetic-tree/graph instances, exact wall-time
lca-bridge-finding|conf/ipps/0001SS21.rationale: This is the sole surveyed paper and the entire basis for this track's spec — its own LCA and bridge sub-benchmarks (synthetic-tree sizes, ground-truth-checked timing) are the spec's only evidence.

lossless-compression|conf/asplos/FanYPLL.regime: LLM weight-tensor operand feeding a downstream GEMM, fused decompress-into-Tensor-Core-registers, GPU
lossless-compression|conf/asplos/FanYPLL.rationale: Headline IS a lossless-compression format (TCA-TBE) + fused decompress-GEMM kernel, reported at kernel level (2.21x over cuBLAS) as well as end-to-end vLLM; this is exactly the structured-operand-fused variant's target case.

lossless-compression|conf/hpdc/KnespelB2.regime: generic byte-stream corpora (Silesia corpus, base64-encoded data), CPU multi-core
lossless-compression|conf/hpdc/KnespelB2.rationale: Rapidgzip's headline IS a parallel gzip/DEFLATE decompressor benchmarked at kernel-level GB/s against GNU gzip on the Silesia corpus, exactly the generic byte-stream CPU variant's target.

lossless-compression|conf/ics/ZhangTDYST.rationale: Headline IS a GPU LZSS lossless compressor specifically designed for multi-byte data, benchmarked at kernel-level throughput/ratio against SOTA GPU compressors.

lossless-compression|conf/ipps/RiveraDTY.regime: SZ/cuSZ quantization-code streams (8 scientific datasets), V100
lossless-compression|conf/ipps/RiveraDTY.rationale: Headline IS an optimization of the Huffman-decoding lossless sub-kernel inside cuSZ, benchmarked at kernel level against cuSZ's own decoder -- exactly the SZ/cuSZ quantization-stream domain this variant's summary names.

lossless-compression|conf/sc/HuangD0Z0J0.regime: unspecified HPC application datasets (five named), CPU multi-core, embedded in an MPI-collective compression-communication co-design
lossless-compression|conf/sc/HuangD0Z0J0.rationale: Abstract frames the lightweight CPU compressor as built 'in addition to' the paper's main contribution (a homomorphic compression-communication co-design for collectives); the compressor is real and separable but a component of the collective-communication system, and the evaluation is dominated by collective speedup, not standalone codec throughput.

lossless-compression|conf/sc/HuangDUMCLS.regime: X-ray light-source detector/sensor integer data, single-kernel GPU compressor, A100
lossless-compression|conf/sc/HuangDUMCLS.rationale: Headline IS a single-kernel GPU lossless/lossy compressor for scientific sensor/detector streams -- the exact HPC-scientific multi-byte-integer domain this variant's summary names explicitly.

lossless-compression|conf/sc/HuangYYLGLJ.regime: multi-byte integer data (adaptive data mapping), CPU and GPU (A100/MI210)
lossless-compression|conf/sc/HuangYYLGLJ.rationale: Headline IS a general multi-byte ANS lossless encoder benchmarked at kernel-level throughput across CPU/GPU, matching the GPU multi-byte-integer variant's scope.

lossy-compression|conf/hpdc/WangPGJTAT22.regime: 3D AMR simulation data, high-dimensional SZ compression per refinement level, CPU
