lossy-compression|conf/hpdc/WangPGJTAT22.rationale: TAC (predecessor of TAC+) is explicitly named as an SZ-family denominator paper the CPU error-bound variant is built around.

lossy-compression|conf/hpdc/YangDZLL00C0.regime: interpolation-based SZ-family error-bounded compression, real-world scientific datasets, progressive/bitplane retrieval, CPU
lossy-compression|conf/hpdc/YangDZLL00C0.rationale: IPComp's headline is an interpolation-based error-bounded lossy compressor (same SZ-family predictor class), evaluated by compression ratio/speed against SOTA progressive compressors on real scientific datasets; CPU only.

lossy-compression|conf/hpdc/ZhangTD0F0TC.rationale: FZ-GPU is explicitly named/used to help define the spec's SDRBench dataset selection and GPU dual-scope variant.

lossy-compression|conf/hpdc/ZhaoDLLTCC20.regime: large-scale HPC simulation datasets, SZ 2nd-order prediction + parameter optimization, CPU/distributed
lossy-compression|conf/hpdc/ZhaoDLLTCC20.rationale: Headline is an SZ-family compression-ratio improvement (2nd-order prediction), evaluated directly by compression ratio and parallel I/O throughput on real HPC datasets; CPU only.

lossy-compression|conf/ics/0006JGTLT22.regime: real-world scientific datasets, SZ-family adaptive lossy compression on FPGA
lossy-compression|conf/ics/0006JGTLT22.rationale: CEAZ's headline is a full FPGA-based error-bounded compressor evaluated with compression ratio/throughput against a prior FPGA compressor; FPGA-only, not GPU.

morphology-image-kernel|conf/cgo/Koehler.regime: Harris corner-response pipeline (grayscale->Sobel->structure tensor->response) on the artifact's own fixed 2-image evaluation set, mobile ARM CPU
morphology-image-kernel|conf/cgo/Koehler.rationale: This is the sole surveyed paper for this track, and the spec's variant is built entirely around its own confirmed protocol (30 timing iterations, median/min/max, the exact 2-image suite); headline is the domain-extensible rewrite-rule compiler generating this Harris kernel and comparing it to Halide/OpenCV.

quantized-gemm|conf/sc/FengWGLD21.regime: arbitrary 1-8 bit GEMM/CONV via INT1 Tensor-Core emulation, fixed synthetic shapes (no real LLM/network beyond small CNNs)

quantized-gemm|conf/sc/LiOH22.regime: quantized (int4/int8) SpMM/SDDMM on sparse pruned DNN weight matrices (DLMC), not dense GEMM

quantized-gemm|conf/sc/WangXY0C25.rationale: MXBLAS is a library whose headline IS the MX-GEMM kernel, evaluated kernel-level; it is the direct source of the spec's qgemm-w8a8-mx variant (including the flush_l2 fairness correction the spec applies to its own default).

quantized-gemm|conf/usenix/XiaZWCYYBWZZR.regime: FP6/arbitrary-bit Tensor-Core GEMM, LLaMA/OPT linear layers, batch {8,16,32}, PPL/zero-shot accuracy reported separately
quantized-gemm|conf/usenix/XiaZWCYYBWZZR.rationale: TC-FPx/Quant-LLM is one of only two papers the spec calls out as treating model-level accuracy as first-class alongside kernel speed, and its batch-crossover finding (0.94x slowdown at batch=32) directly motivated the spec's batched-kernel variant.

quantized-gemm|conf/usenix/ZhangZSZ25.regime: Qtile-graph compiler generating quantized LLM GEMM kernels, matrix-size and bit-width sweeps, kernel+e2e split by GPU
quantized-gemm|conf/usenix/ZhangZSZ25.rationale: QFactory is a compilation framework (Qtile/QGraph abstraction) that generates quantized kernels among a transformable search space, fitting the compiler/DSL component rule; its AE README's matrix-size/bit-width ablations and Marlin/BitBLAS baselines closely match the spec's suite.

quantized-gemm|journals/tpds/LiS21.regime: 1-bit XNOR/bit-tensor-core GEMM+convolution for Binarized Neural Networks, ResNet-18/ImageNet
quantized-gemm|journals/tpds/LiS21.rationale: TCBNN's headline is a bit-GEMM/bit-conv kernel evaluated kernel-level (ResNet-18 images/sec), but it is native 1-bit XNOR-popcount arithmetic with no dequantize-to-fp16 step at all, the extreme end of the bit-serial family the spec's fairness notes exclude from its mandatory variants (the survey lists it only as APNN-TC's baseline, not deeply surveyed).

quantized-gemm|journals/tpds/WangRLS22.regime: 8-bit integer TRAINING (fwd+bwd+update) with per-layer block scaling on MNIST/CIFAR/ImageNet CNNs, GPU+FPGA
quantized-gemm|journals/tpds/WangRLS22.rationale: NITI's evaluation is a full training loop on small vision CNNs, not isolated inference-GEMM kernel time; the spec's own evidence entry states it is explicitly out of scope for this inference-GEMM track (training, non-LLM shapes).

scan-reduction|conf/asplos/TangLWSLXZL26.regime: online-softmax-then-GEMM cascaded reduction, GPU (A10/H800 per survey)
scan-reduction|conf/asplos/TangLWSLXZL26.rationale: RedFuser's headline methodology IS generalized cascaded-reduction fusion (of which softmax-then-GEMM is the canonical instance), evaluated at kernel level (2-5x over compilers, matching hand-written kernels); this matches the scan-reduction-fused-cascaded variant almost exactly. scan-reduction|conf/sc/HenriksenHSO20.rationale: Headline is exactly generalized-histogram GPU codegen; explicitly named as defining the spec's scan-reduction-segmented-histogram variant.

scan-reduction|journals/tpds/NavarroCBRV.regime: flat sum-reduction over large GPU-resident arrays, GPU
scan-reduction|journals/tpds/NavarroCBRV.rationale: Headline is exactly a tensor-core arithmetic-reduction kernel; explicitly named as defining the spec's scan-reduction-flat-kernel variant.

sddmm|conf/asplos/JainGC25.regime: CPU adaptive-tiling sparse kernels on 47 named SuiteSparse matrices overlapping RoDe's suite
sddmm|conf/asplos/JainGC25.rationale: RASSM's own abstract frames its headline speedup entirely in SpMM terms with SDDMM as a secondary code path (--kernel sddmm exists but is SpMM-adjacent per the spec's open_questions), so SDDMM is real but not the paper's headline; its SuiteSparse selection matches the general-suite variant's input tradition closely.

sddmm|conf/asplos/WonAAE26.regime: unverified — claims tensor-core sparse GPU kernels (SpMM/SDDMM/sparse einsum) via an indirect-einsum compiler; artifact not yet recoverable
sddmm|conf/asplos/WonAAE26.rationale: Insum is a compiler generating multiple sparse-kernel types (SpMM/SDDMM/general sparse einsum), fitting the DSL-generates-this-kernel component rule; the spec's own evidence/open_questions state the artifact repo is an unrelated demo with no benchmark scripts recoverable since ASPLOS'26 has not yet occurred, so regime fit is genuinely unconfirmed.

sddmm|conf/asplos/YeLSCC23.regime: composable sparse tensor compiler generating GNN/SDDMM/sparse-attention/sparse-conv operators vs vendor libraries
sddmm|conf/asplos/YeLSCC23.rationale: SparseTIR is a general sparse tensor compiler whose example set includes SDDMM among several kernel types (SpMM, sparse attention, sparse conv), matching the DSL/compiler component rule; it was not one of the 10 papers deep-surveyed for this spec so its exact suite overlap with the SuiteSparse/DLMC/GNN traditions is unconfirmed, only loosely similar (GNN-operator/vendor-library framing).

sddmm|conf/ics/DiasSS022.regime: unverified — CPU loop-nest-restructuring compiler (TACO extension) with SDDMM as one example operator
sddmm|conf/ics/DiasSS022.rationale: SparseLNR is a general sparse-tensor-algebra scheduling/codegen system (compiler/DSL component rule applies) with SDDMM as one of several example kernels; it was not deep-surveyed for this spec, is CPU-only, and TACO-family benchmarks typically diverge from this track's SuiteSparse/DLMC/GNN-graph traditions, so regime is marked mismatch on current evidence.

sddmm|conf/ics/LiC25.regime: fused SDDMM+softmax+SpMM sparse attention on real GNN graphs (cora/pubmed/reddit/ogbn-*), K=128, tensor cores
sddmm|conf/ics/LiC25.rationale: Fused3S is the direct model for both the tensorcore-blocked-fp16 and attention-e2e variants — the spec calls its protocol 'the cleanest in the track' and reuses its exact warmup/rep/statistic and 3-term FLOP formula.

sddmm|conf/ipps/BharadwajBD22.regime: distributed-memory 1.5D/2.5D SDDMM+SpMM on synthetic Erdos-Renyi matrices, MPI/CPU cluster
sddmm|conf/ipps/BharadwajBD22.rationale: FusedMM/HnH's headline IS a distributed communication-eliding SDDMM+SpMM kernel evaluated kernel-level (GFLOP/s vs PETSc/MKL), but the spec's own notes_on_fairness explicitly says its min-wall-time dynamic-repetition protocol on synthetic ER matrices is structurally different from every fixed-rep GPU variant and is NOT folded into any of them.

sddmm|conf/ipps/FanWC23.regime: hybrid-parallel SpMM/SDDMM for GNN training, 16 named GNN graphs (Yelp/Flickr/.../reddit), K in {32,64,128}
sddmm|conf/ipps/FanWC23.rationale: Paper/title claim a fused hybrid-parallel SpMM+SDDMM kernel evaluated kernel-level (GFLOPS) on a real-GNN-graph suite matching the tensorcore-blocked-fp16 tradition; flagged as a hard call because the spec's own open_questions note the currently hosted artifact snapshot contains only an SpMM benchmark path, no verifiable SDDMM code despite the paper/repo title.

sddmm|conf/ipps/RahmanSA21.regime: unified vectorized SDDMM-SpMM on real graphs (Cora/Pubmed/YouTube/Orkut/OGBprot) for graph embedding, CPU/ARM
sddmm|conf/ipps/RahmanSA21.rationale: FusedMM is named explicitly as a source paper for the sddmm-attention-e2e variant (its Force2Vec end-to-end runs) and its real-graph suite closely matches the tensorcore-blocked-fp16 input tradition, though its own correctness check is only an indirect downstream F1-score match, not a numerical tolerance.

sddmm|conf/ppopp/PangFQZL24.regime: row-decomposition CSR SpMM/SDDMM on SuiteSparse matrices selected by rows/cols/nnz thresholds
sddmm|conf/ppopp/PangFQZL24.rationale: RoDe is the literal source of the sddmm-csr-kernel-f32 variant — the spec copies RoDe's own ssgetpy filter verbatim for its matrix suite.

sddmm|conf/ppopp/ShiLXFWW25.regime: SpMM/SDDMM on 515 SuiteSparse matrices + DGL/PyG GNN graphs, fp16/tf32 tensor-core blocked format
sddmm|conf/ppopp/ShiLXFWW25.rationale: FlashSparse is named explicitly in the spec's tensorcore-blocked-fp16 claim text ('matches FlashSparse's and Fused3S's own kernel-only tables') and its dual fp16/tf32 rows and format-conversion ablation map directly onto the variant's protocol.

sddmm|conf/sc/GaleZYE20.regime: DLMC sparse-DNN weights + SuiteSparse, fp32/mixed-fp16, foundational Sputnik kernel library
sddmm|conf/sc/GaleZYE20.rationale: Gale et al./Sputnik is explicitly named as the common-denominator kernel every later paper in this track baselines against, and it spans both the DLMC and general-SuiteSparse traditions the spec's variants are built around.

sddmm|conf/sc/LiOH22.regime: quantized (4b/8b/16b) SDDMM on DLMC sparse-DNN weight matrices at controlled sparsity buckets
sddmm|conf/sc/LiOH22.rationale: Magicube is the direct source of the sddmm-quantized-dlmc variant — the spec's sparsity-bucket file lists and precision rows are taken straight from Magicube's own eval_matrices/s*.txt convention.

sddmm|conf/usenix/WangFWHD23.regime: SpMM/SDDMM on real GNN graphs mapped to tensor cores via sparse-graph translation, vs DGL
sddmm|conf/usenix/WangFWHD23.rationale: TC-GNN's headline is a manual kernel-translation design for SpMM+SDDMM on tensor cores and it is cited as a standard kernel-level baseline by peer papers in this exact track (FlashSparse's baseline list); it was not deep-surveyed here so its exact graph suite/precision overlap with the tensorcore-blocked-fp16 variant is unconfirmed.

sequence-alignment|conf/ipps/MullerS0MLK.regime: DNA long-sequence pairs, exact Smith-Waterman/Needleman-Wunsch, CPU/GPU/FPGA
sequence-alignment|conf/ipps/MullerS0MLK.rationale: AnySeq's headline is a general high-performance pairwise-alignment library evaluated at kernel level against SeqAn/NVBio; explicitly named as defining part of the spec's exact-pairwise variant.

sequence-alignment|conf/ipps/ZeniGEDSHBO.regime: synthetic long-read pairs (LOGAN's own scenario) + E. coli/C. elegans real subsets, X-drop approximate, GPU

sequence-alignment|journals/tpds/Figueir.regime: long DNA sequence pairs (whole chromosomes), exact Smith-Waterman, multi-GPU

signed-graph-balancing|conf/sc/AlabandiT.regime: linear-time vertex/edge-labeling fundamental-cycle balancing on SNAP signed-graphs + Amazon rating graphs, CUDA+OpenMP

sparse-attention-kernel|conf/ipps/Tomcza.regime: structured sparse-attention masks, swept sparsity factor, GPU

sparse-attention-kernel|conf/ppopp/DaiDR.rationale: STOF's 5 named mask types directly define the spec's sparse-attn-structured-mask-kernel variant.

sparse-factorization|journals/tpds/Gaihr.regime: symbolic LU factorization of nonsymmetric sparse matrices, GPU (scaled to multi-node Summit)
sparse-factorization|journals/tpds/Gaihr.rationale: gSoFa's headline IS specifically the symbolic-factorization step of sparse LU, matching the spec's dedicated sparse-factor-symbolic-kernel variant exactly.

sparse-factorization|journals/tpds/LiLYL.regime: sparse SPD Cholesky factorization on real matrices, Sunway many-core CPU
sparse-factorization|journals/tpds/LiLYL.rationale: swCholesky's headline IS sparse Cholesky factorization (supernode task queues + auto-tuning), matching the numeric-kernel factorization variant; no GPU.

sparse-tensor-contraction|conf/asplos/Wo.regime: sparse(-structured/unstructured)-times-dense indirect-einsum GPU kernels (structured SpMM, unstructured SpMM, point-cloud sparse conv, equivariant tensor product), fp32/fp16, single NVIDIA GPU

sparse-tensor-contraction|conf/ics/DiasS.rationale: SparseLNR is the sole and literal basis for the spec's composite-fused-sparse-tensor-algebra-kernel variant, whose 14-matrix/5-tensor suite is drawn directly from this paper's own evaluation set.

sparse-tensor-contraction|journals/tpds/.rationale: parTC is the sole and literal basis for the spec's sparse-sparse-tensor-contraction-frostt-kernel-fp64 variant, whose recommended_subset (nips, uber, chicago-crime, etc.) is drawn directly from parTC's own worked examples.

spatial-join|conf/ics/GengLZ24.regime: RT-core-accelerated line-segment-intersection + point-in-polygon spatial join on real geospatial polygon datasets
spatial-join|conf/ics/GengLZ24.rationale: RayJoin is the sole surveyed paper and the direct, entire basis for this track's spec (grid/lbvh/rt modes, build-vs-query split, cuSpatial baseline all drawn straight from its own artifact).

spectral-sparsification|conf/dac/Aghdaei.regime: incremental spectral sparsification, SuiteSparse Laplacian-derived graphs, CPU
spectral-sparsification|conf/dac/Aghdaei.rationale: inGRASS's headline IS the incremental spectral-sparsification algorithm itself (LRD decomposition + resistance-embedding updates), the sole and direct basis for both variants, matching the paper's own 200x speedup claim. CPU only.

spgemm|conf/ics/BellavitaPPVG26.rationale: Trident's headline is exactly a distributed communication-avoiding SpGEMM algorithm; its own Table 2 workloads define the spec's distributed-strong-scaling variant. Multi-GPU/multi-node is the point of the paper.

spgemm|conf/ics/LiG26.regime: SuiteSparse square/rectangular matrices, fp64, single GPU
spgemm|conf/ics/LiG26.rationale: Ocean's headline is a single-GPU estimation-based SpGEMM kernel replacing the symbolic pass; explicitly named as one of the papers defining the spec's flop-threshold selection and square-kernel variant.

spgemm|conf/ipps/BellavitaRICDVG26.regime: kernel-matrix / clustering-derived sparse operands for distributed Kernel K-means, not general A^2 self-products

spgemm|conf/ipps/HussainSBA21.rationale: Headline is exactly communication-avoiding, memory-constrained distributed SpGEMM at extreme scale in CombBLAS; explicitly one of the papers whose Table V instances define the spec's distributed-strong-scaling variant.

spgemm|conf/ipps/LiuFAALJPG22.regime: hypergraph line-graph expansion, not a general A^2 self-product; CPU
spgemm|conf/ipps/LiuFAALJPG22.rationale: The paper's own algorithms are explicitly designed to be 'orders of magnitude faster than state-of-the-art SpGEMM methods' by avoiding SpGEMM -- SpGEMM appears only as the baseline class the paper beats, not as an optimized kernel of this work.

spgemm|conf/ppopp/BellavitaPMVG25.regime: kernel-matrix operands for GPU Kernel K-means, not general A^2 self-products
spgemm|conf/ppopp/BellavitaPMVG25.rationale: Popcorn formulates Kernel K-means via sparse linear algebra (including SpGEMM-like primitives) as an internal building block; evaluation is end-to-end clustering time, not isolated SpGEMM throughput vs SpGEMM competitors.

spgemm|conf/ppopp/NiuLJS0022.regime: SuiteSparse matrices (A^2, general A x B), fp64, GPU
spgemm|conf/ppopp/NiuLJS0022.rationale: TileSpGEMM's headline is exactly a general tiled GPU SpGEMM algorithm addressing load imbalance/locality/accumulator selection; one of the deeply-surveyed papers that directly defines the spec's square-kernel variant.

spgemm|conf/sc/Islam00B25.rationale: clusterwise-spgemm's headline is exactly an SpGEMM row-reordering + cluster-wise computation scheme; its own break-even-iteration methodology directly defines the spec's e2e-preproc variant. CPU-only.

spgemm|conf/sc/LuZWFLCY0C024.regime: tensor-core mixed-precision R.A.P coarsening products from AMG's own hierarchy, not a benchmark-chosen A^2
spgemm|conf/sc/LuZWFLCY0C024.rationale: Per benchspecs/spgemm/survey.md, AmgT's SpGEMM is 'not a standalone SpGEMM microbenchmark' -- it is measured as it naturally occurs inside AMG setup (R_i.A.P_i per level), an AMG-workload-weighted mixture rather than a clean kernel-level A^2 measurement; validated only via AMG solve convergence, not elementwise SpGEMM correctness.

spgemm|journals/tpds/AzadSHGB22.rationale: CombBLAS 2.0 is a general distributed combinatorial-algorithms library covering many primitives (SpGEMM one of them); evaluated via library-wide scaling/application rules-of-thumb rather than a dedicated SpGEMM-vs-SOTA kernel benchmark. spgemm|journals/tpds/ChenY25.rationale: ToT reformulates triangle counting as SpGEMM+intersection+reduction on tensor cores, but the paper's headline and evaluation metric are end-to-end triangle-counting speedup/memory savings, not general-purpose fp64 A^2 SpGEMM throughput; operates on boolean graph matrices rather than general SuiteSparse values.

spgemm|journals/tpds/SinghU25.rationale: parTC's contribution is sparse tensor contraction (SpGETT) that deliberately AVOIDS the SpGEMM-based approach, using SpGEMM only as a comparison baseline it outperforms.

spiking-neural-network|journals/tpds/QuZ.rationale: The spec's snn-lif-sim-throughput variant explicitly matches BSim's own test harness and GeNN comparison points.

spmm|conf/asplos/JainGC25.rationale: RASSM's residue-based adaptive tiling is evaluated with dedicated SpMM-specific GFLOPS/median-time numbers against MKL/ASpT/J-Stream/CSF-4; spec's CPU variant (RASSM's own median-of-50 protocol) is explicitly modeled on this paper.

spmm|conf/asplos/WonAAE26.rationale: Insum is a general indirect-Einsum compiler (SpMM/SDDMM/sparse-einsum all generated by the same lowering); README shows an SpMM-COO example but no named benchmark matrix suite, so it generates this kernel among others rather than being an SpMM-specific implementation.

spmm|conf/asplos/YeLSCC23.regime: standard GNN operator benchmark graphs, evaluated via a composable-format compiler generating SpMM/SDDMM/sparse-attention/sparse-conv kernels
spmm|conf/asplos/YeLSCC23.rationale: SparseTIR is a sparse tensor compiler whose search space spans multiple operator classes (GNN ops, sparse attention, sparse conv); SpMM is one operator family among several the compiler targets and tunes, matching the compiler/DSL 'generates this kernel among others' case.

spmm|conf/cgo/FuRH24.regime: CPU multi-core SpMM vs Intel MKL, fp32
spmm|conf/cgo/FuRH24.rationale: JITSpMM's whole contribution is a JIT-codegen technique specifically for the SpMM kernel, benchmarked at kernel level against MKL's SpMM routine.

spmm|conf/dac/HuangLQSDX22.regime: block-structured (Shfl-BW) pruned DNN weight matrices, tunable density (e.g. 10%), Tensor-Core GEMM benchmark vs dense baseline, V100/T4/A100
spmm|conf/dac/HuangLQSDX22.rationale: README confirms a genuine standalone kernel benchmark (benchmark.spmm.out, A x B with a chosen block-sparsity density) rather than an end-to-end system, but the sparsity pattern is structured block-wise pruning for DNN weights, not the spec's general unstructured SuiteSparse fp32 regime.

spmm|conf/hpdc/FuJH22.regime: real GNN graphs, two-level (vertex/feature) parallel aggregation kernel evaluated end-to-end against full GNN computation systems (DGL/GNNAdvisor/FeatGraph)
spmm|conf/hpdc/FuJH22.rationale: TLPGNN's SpMM-like aggregation redesign is real and separable, but every reported number (5.6x/7.7x/3.3x) is a comparison against complete GNN computation systems, not standalone kernel throughput vs. a vendor/kernel library.

spmm|conf/hpdc/PengTPK25.regime: general SuiteSparse-style sparse matrices vs cuSPARSE/Sputnik/dgSPARSE/TACO, fp32
spmm|conf/hpdc/PengTPK25.rationale: LiteForm's CELL format and its auto-composition system are evaluated as a general SpMM kernel with GFLOPS speedups over cuSPARSE/Sputnik/dgSPARSE/TACO, not tied to any one downstream application.

spmm|conf/ics/DezfuliC25.regime: GNN training graphs (via PyG) and sparse-solve matrices (via MKL), CPU tile-fused loop kernels
spmm|conf/ics/DezfuliC25.rationale: Tile fusion is a compiler technique that fuses SpMM tiles with an adjacent parallel loop (GNN aggregation or sparse triangular solve); SpMM is one of the loop shapes it fuses/generates, and speedups are reported for the fused GNN-training and sparse-solve pipelines, not an isolated SpMM benchmark.

spmm|conf/ics/DiasSS022.regime: mixed corpus (SuiteSparse + Network Repository + FROSTT + DARPA1998), CPU 64-core, TACO-generated fused loop-nest kernels
spmm|conf/ics/DiasSS022.rationale: SparseLNR is a compiler (loop-nest restructuring for TACO) that generates fused kernels for multiple sparse tensor expressions, of which 2D SpMM (pdb1HYS, circuit5M, cora, bcsstk17) is one instance among 3D-tensor and other expressions.

spmm|conf/ics/LiC25.regime: real-world graph datasets (single and batched graphs) feeding a fused SDDMM+softmax+SpMM sparse-attention pipeline, H100/A30
spmm|conf/ics/LiC25.rationale: SpMM here is one of three fused steps (3S) inside a sparse-attention kernel, evaluated as the fused pipeline and end-to-end Graph Transformer inference rather than as a standalone SpMM vs. cuSPARSE-class baseline.

spmm|conf/ics/ShenBSCH26.regime: unstructured-sparse pruned LLM weights, ~30-90% density, fp16/bf16 Tensor Cores via CDP-TCBE bitmap decoding
spmm|conf/ics/ShenBSCH26.rationale: Headline is an SpMM kernel (CDP-TCBE format) but built and evaluated for LLM inference weight sparsity; spec's general variant is SuiteSparse fp32, only the tensorcore-fp16 variant is in range.

spmm|conf/ipps/AlvesMBFGR25.regime: binary (0/1) real-graph adjacency matrices for GNN inference, CPU shared-memory serial/parallel
spmm|conf/ipps/AlvesMBFGR25.rationale: CBM's headline contribution IS a compressed format + kernel for binary-matrix times dense-matrix multiplication, benchmarked directly against SOTA sparse-dense kernels; but it only handles 0/1-valued matrices, narrower than the spec's general real-valued SuiteSparse/GNN suite.

spmm|conf/ipps/BharadwajBD22.regime: Erdos-Renyi random matrices + large real sparse matrices (100M+ edges), 256-node Cray XC40 CPU cluster, 1.5D/2.5D distributed communication-eliding algorithms vs PETSc
spmm|conf/ipps/BharadwajBD22.rationale: Headline IS distributed SpMM/SDDMM algorithms evaluated against PETSc's SpMM kernel, but the metric and scale (256-node communication time) are the distributed regime the spec explicitly separates from single-node kernel throughput.

spmm|conf/ipps/FanWC23.regime: sparse matrices from real GNN applications, kernel-level plus embedded in GCN full-graph and GraphSAINT sampling training
spmm|conf/ipps/FanWC23.rationale: HP-SpMM/HP-SDDMM are new standalone GPU kernels (hybrid vertex/edge parallelism) directly benchmarked against SOTA sparse kernel implementations before being embedded into GNN frameworks.

spmm|conf/ipps/MaWDCH0ZWZCDWFP25.regime: N:M structured sparsity (e.g. 2:4/4:8 patterns), dense-format block matmul vs nmSPARSE and cuBLAS dense GEMM
spmm|conf/ipps/MaWDCH0ZWZCDWFP25.rationale: NM-SpMM's headline is a general N:M-sparse matmul kernel evaluated at kernel level against nmSPARSE/cuBLAS, but N:M structured sparsity is a narrower regime than the spec's unstructured SuiteSparse/GNN headline.

spmm|conf/ipps/RahmanSA21.regime: named real graphs (Cora..Orkut) + synthetic RMAT, 3 CPU architectures, fp32, MKL SpMM-only baseline plus DGL
spmm|conf/ipps/RahmanSA21.rationale: Per survey.md #2 and spec.yaml's own cpu-kernel-f32 claim text, FusedMM is explicitly cited as one of the papers this CPU variant is modeled on; the paper isolates SpMM against an MKL SpMM-only baseline even though the kernel is fused with SDDMM for its primary use case.

spmm|conf/ppopp/GianinazziZHLAS24.regime: 13 of the largest SuiteSparse matrices decomposed into arrow matrices, 100+ nodes / 128-GPU distributed scale, communication-volume metric not throughput
spmm|conf/ppopp/GianinazziZHLAS24.rationale: Headline IS a sparse-dense-matmul algorithm (arrow decomposition) evaluated against a prior SpMM algorithm, but at distributed multi-node/multi-GPU scale with communication volume as the metric; spec's notes_on_fairness explicitly excludes distributed SpMM as incommensurable with the single-node kernel variants.

spmm|conf/ppopp/PangFQZL24.rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #8): RoDe cleanly separates preprocessing from the per-call kernel and reports GFLOP/s against Sputnik/cuSPARSE on SuiteSparse; this is the paper the spec's kernel-f32 variant is built around.

spmm|conf/ppopp/ShiLXFWW25.regime: SuiteSparse/GNN matrices in the RoDe/DTC-SpMM comparison lineage, tensor-core, H100/RTX4090
spmm|conf/ppopp/ShiLXFWW25.rationale: FlashSparse is a general tensor-core SpMM/SDDMM kernel technique with geometric-mean speedups directly against RoDe and DTC-SpMM, the same matrix families those two use.

spmm|conf/sc/0003HLQGW0LG020.regime: tile-wise structured sparsity, pruned DNN weight matrices, GPU tensor core, compared only against the dense model (no SpMM-library baseline)
spmm|conf/sc/0003HLQGW0LG020.rationale: Headline IS a co-designed sparse-matmul kernel/pattern, evaluated at kernel level, but on structured tile-wise DNN-pruning sparsity rather than the spec's general unstructured SuiteSparse regime, and against a dense baseline rather than SpMM libraries.

spmm|conf/sc/CheshmiCD22.regime: CPU vectorized SpMM (alongside SpMV/SpTRSV) vs Intel MKL
spmm|conf/sc/CheshmiCD22.rationale: LCM I/E's codelet-mining vectorization reports a dedicated SpMM speedup (1.75x avg) against MKL among its three target kernels, a genuine kernel-level comparison.

spmm|conf/sc/DongS0LXHZ025.regime: SuiteSparse/GNN matrices (same family RoDe/DTC-SpMM use), transformed via matching+padding into 2:4 structured Sparse Tensor Core layout
spmm|conf/sc/DongS0LXHZ025.rationale: MP-SpMM's headline is converting general unstructured SpMM into structured 2:4 sparsity and is benchmarked directly against RoDe/DTC-SpMM; the underlying matrices match the spec's suite but the executed format is structured Sparse-Tensor-Core, not the spec's general unstructured fp32/fp16 kernel.

spmm|conf/sc/GaleZYE20.regime: DNN-pruned weight matrices (3,012 matrices from real pruned ResNet-50/Transformer models via magnitude pruning, moderate ~70-95% sparsity), fp32 primary + fp16-mixed variant, V100
spmm|conf/sc/GaleZYE20.rationale: Per survey.md #1, headline IS a general SpMM/SDDMM GPU kernel library (ancestor of Sputnik, later used as a baseline throughout this track) evaluated at kernel level vs cuSPARSE, but its own test corpus is DNN-pruned moderate-sparsity weight matrices, not SuiteSparse-class matrices.

spmm|conf/sc/HeLDL0M025.regime: GNN adjacency graphs (15 benchmark datasets), evaluated end-to-end against GCN training frameworks (GNNAdvisor/PyG/DGL), no cuSPARSE/kernel-library baseline reported
spmm|conf/sc/HeLDL0M025.rationale: StraGCN's Strassen-based SpMM is real and separable, but every reported speedup (2.1-3.3x) is against full GCN training frameworks rather than a standalone kernel vs. a vendor/kernel-level baseline.

spmm|conf/sc/HuYWYZL0ZW20.regime: real GNN graphs, composable sparse-templates+UDF backend generating GNN aggregation kernels, CPU and GPU
spmm|conf/sc/HuYWYZL0ZW20.rationale: FeatGraph is a flexible backend that composes coarse-grained sparse templates with user-defined functions to generate various GNN aggregation kernels (of which SpMM-style aggregation is one instance), evaluated via end-to-end GNN training/inference speedup.

spmm|conf/sc/HuangD0Y20.regime: SNAP graph collection + misc SuiteSparse-like matrices, CSR-native, fp32, N in {32..512}
spmm|conf/sc/HuangD0Y20.rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #7): ITER=200 batched CUDA-event GFLOP/s vs cuSPARSE/Gunrock, the classic kernel-level SpMM benchmark this spec's variant descends from.

spmm|conf/sc/LiOH22.regime: quantized int4/int8/mixed-precision SpMM on Tensor Cores, A100
spmm|conf/sc/LiOH22.rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #11): Magicube is the paper the spmm-gpu-quantized-int variant is modeled on, with per-iteration CUDA-event timing and an exact-match integer reference.

spmm|conf/sc/OkanovicKLBVH24.regime: 9 curated SuiteSparse matrices (matrix_list.csv: mip1, shipsec1, pdb1HYS, consph, cant, cop20k_A, dc2, rma10, conf5_4-8x8-10), A100, M=N=K=512
spmm|conf/sc/OkanovicKLBVH24.rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #10): SMaT's own matrix list is exactly the recommended_subset's SuiteSparse cluster, benchmarked at kernel level via the raw MMA API against DASP/cuSPARSE/Magicube.

spmm|conf/sc/TripathyYB20.regime: Reddit + >1B-edge protein network, Summit >100 GPUs; wraps an unmodified cuSPARSE local SpMM kernel -- the contribution is the distributed communication schedule around it, not the kernel
spmm|conf/sc/TripathyYB20.rationale: Per survey.md #6, the paper's own text notes 'the SpMM kernel itself is not novel here, the contribution is the communication schedule'; CAGNET calls cuSPARSE via PyTorch without optimizing it, matching the 'kernel only touched, never optimized' tangential case.

spmm|conf/usenix/WangFWHD23.regime: GNN benchmark graphs (the TC-GNN/GNNAdvisor lineage the spec's recommended_subset traces back to), evaluated primarily as DGL-framework training speedup rather than standalone GFLOP/s
spmm|conf/usenix/WangFWHD23.rationale: TC-GNN's sparse-graph-translation kernel is the ancestor of the exact 8-graph GNN suite this track's spec cites, and DTC-SpMM's own artifact runs TC-GNN's kernel as one of its parallel kernel-level baselines, evidencing a genuine separable SpMM/SDDMM kernel even though TC-GNN's own abstract reports only DGL-framework-level speedup.

spmm|conf/usenix/WangGXCT25.regime: pruned LLM weight matrices AND the SuiteSparse collection (per README's matrix_example/{pruned_weight,suite_collection}), kernel-level vs cuSPARSE, fp32 with an optional half-precision path
spmm|conf/usenix/WangGXCT25.rationale: README confirms GeneralSparse benchmarks both pruned-LLM weights and genuine SuiteSparse .mtx matrices at kernel level against cuSPARSE (not just an LLM afterthought), so the general fp32 GPU-kernel variant is directly covered alongside the LLM-pruning niche.

spmm|conf/usenix/XiaWY0C25.regime: SuiteSparse/GNN benchmark matrices in the RoDe/DTC-SpMM/TC-GNN comparison lineage, fp32/tensor-core, unverified beyond convention
spmm|conf/usenix/XiaWY0C25.rationale: Voltrix is a general tensor-core SpMM kernel design (async loading, I/O-balanced partitioning) benchmarked directly against TC-GNN/DTC-SpMM/RoDe, the same comparison family DTC-SpMM's own artifact uses.

spmm|journals/tpds/XuSYLJ22.regime: GNN training graphs (Cora..YouTube, 10-80% training-vertex ratio), backward-aggregation-only partial-vertex SpMM isolated inside the full training-loop decomposition
spmm|journals/tpds/XuSYLJ22.rationale: Per survey.md #4, EPPGCN's own framing is explicit: SpMM/aggregation time is 'one component reported separately from total epoch time' of a whole-training-loop decomposition, not a standalone kernel microbenchmark, and it targets only the partial-vertex backward-aggregation sub-case.

spmm|journals/tpds/XueWYTLFSCSL25.regime: 3,000+ sparse matrices from established SuiteSparse-scale collections, 4 generations of Tensor Cores, structured+unstructured sparsity
spmm|journals/tpds/XueWYTLFSCSL25.rationale: SSpMM is a general tensor-core SpMM library benchmarked at kernel level across a very large matrix collection against the SOTA SpMM solution, squarely the spec's headline claim.

spmspv|conf/ics/ElbekK26.regime: real-world graph BFS-frontier density trajectory, tensor-core bitwise-tile batched SpMSpV
spmspv|conf/ics/ElbekK26.rationale: SpMSpV is a compute-level technique inside BLEST's larger tensor-core BFS pipeline, not the paper's headline; explicitly the anchor for the spec's spmspv-bfs-frontier-trace variant.

spmspv|journals/tpds/LiAY21.regime: SuiteSparse matrices, swept input-vector density, GPU kernel-selection framework
spmspv|journals/tpds/LiAY21.rationale: Explicitly the central anchor for the spec's spmspv-density-sweep-kernel variant ('the controlled-sensitivity-curve variant LiAY21 runs directly'); SpMSpV is one of the two co-headline kernels.

spmv|conf/asplos/JainGC25.rationale: Per benchspecs/spmv/survey.md #10, RASSM's abstract advertises SpMV/SpTS among its SSMKs but the public artifact's kernel dispatch only implements spmm/sddmm; a repo-wide search for spmv returns zero hits, so it is excluded from the spmv spec entirely.

spmv|conf/dac/LinLDZLY25.regime: general SuiteSparse-style sparse matrices, multi-core CPU
spmv|conf/dac/LinLDZLY25.rationale: SSpMV's headline is an ML-based algorithm/parameter selector specifically for SpMV, evaluated at kernel level against SOTA sparse libraries across multi-core platforms; CPU-only.

spmv|conf/dac/ParraviciniCSS21.regime: mostly synthetic embedding-similarity matrices (+1 real GloVe matrix), reduced/fixed-point precision, FPGA
spmv|conf/dac/ParraviciniCSS21.rationale: Top-K SpMV fuses a top-k reduction into the SpMV kernel for approximate embedding similarity search -- a distinct operation from the spec's plain y=Ax, evaluated with ranking-quality metrics (not elementwise tolerance) on mostly-synthetic data; FPGA-only.

spmv|conf/dac/SongCGC22.regime: general SuiteSparse Matrix Collection (2,519 matrices, geomean density 1.4e-3), fp32, FPGA
spmv|conf/dac/SongCGC22.rationale: Serpens's headline is a general-purpose HBM FPGA SpMV accelerator evaluated on the near-exhaustive SuiteSparse suite vs GraphLily/Sextans/K80 GPU at kernel level ('Kernel time' explicitly labeled in code); FPGA-only artifact.

spmv|conf/hpdc/ChuHDDC0WH23.rationale: Headline is two new general-purpose GPU SpMV algorithms (flat/line-enhance) with adaptive selection, evaluated directly against existing GPU SpMV approaches.

spmv|conf/ics/ChunduryBLSM26.regime: diagonal-structured Hamiltonian matrices (HamLib suite), custom diagonal-sparse layout, not general CSR
spmv|conf/ics/ChunduryBLSM26.rationale: HamSim builds a diagonal-sparse matvec kernel but the headline contribution and evaluation are the full Hamiltonian-simulation speedup vs Qiskit-Aer, not isolated y=Ax throughput vs SpMV libraries; the diagonal-only structure and quantum-sim workload (HamLib) differ fundamentally from SuiteSparse.

spmv|conf/ics/CongSC00Q25.regime: SuiteSparse Matrix Collection (2,843 matrices), fp64, GPU
spmv|conf/ics/CongSC00Q25.rationale: CB-SpMV's headline is a cache-friendly blocked SpMV kernel evaluated on 2,843 SuiteSparse matrices vs cuSPARSE-BSR/TileSpMV/DASP, kernel-level throughput on A100/RTX4090; survey confirms fp64 kernel-only timing.

spmv|conf/ics/ZhangWCMWEM23.regime: SuiteSparse SpMV datasets ('smaller'/'larger' tiers), fp, GPU
spmv|conf/ics/ZhangWCMWEM23.rationale: PERKS's headline is a general persistent-kernel execution model demonstrated primarily on 2D/3D stencils, with a Krylov-subspace CG/SpMV instantiation as a secondary generality demonstration; it does report isolated SpMV speedups on SuiteSparse subsets vs a SOTA library.

spmv|conf/ipps/ChenSSTBL22.rationale: Bit-GraphBLAS reports explicit kernel-level SpMV speedups (up to 40x) for its B2SR bit-level format, but per benchspecs/spmv/survey.md this 521-matrix binary domain is explicitly excluded from the general fp SpMV variant since 1-bit storage changes the byte-accounting model.

spmv|conf/ipps/NiuLDJ0T21.rationale: TileSpMV's headline is a general tiled GPU SpMV algorithm evaluated across the full SuiteSparse collection vs Merge-SpMV/CSR5/BSR at kernel level.

spmv|conf/ipps/NoackKK25.regime: SuiteSparse + synthetic Poisson matrices, on IPU (not NVIDIA GPU)
spmv|conf/ipps/NoackKK25.rationale: A DSL/framework (CodeDSL/TensorDSL) that generates a suite of solvers (SpMV, ILU, PBiCGStab) for Graphcore IPUs -- SpMV is one generated kernel among several, though isolated SpMV scaling numbers on SuiteSparse are reported; platform is IPU, not an NVIDIA GPU.

spmv|conf/ipps/YeHHLLJ22.regime: CT-imaging / integral-equation-derived sparse matrices, fp32, CPU SIMD
spmv|conf/ipps/YeHHLLJ22.rationale: CSCV's headline is a new SpMV format+vectorized-kernel evaluated at kernel level against 7 SOTA SpMV implementations, but the test matrices are domain-specific (CT-imaging/integral-equation derived) rather than the track's general SuiteSparse suite -- narrower emphasis than the general variant.

spmv|conf/ipps/ZhangLYDYLW23.regime: sequence of SpMV calls (Ax, A^2x, ..., linear combinations) on the same matrix, SuiteSparse-class, CPU (ARM+Intel)
spmv|conf/ipps/ZhangLYDYLW23.rationale: FBMPK's headline is exactly optimizing a bounded sequence of SpMV invocations on the same matrix; explicitly named in the spec as the paper defining the spmv-sequence-krylov variant.

spmv|conf/sc/CheshmiCD22.rationale: LCM I/E's vectorization technique targets a family of sparse kernels (SpMV/SpMM/SpTRSV) with an explicit, separately-reported SpMV speedup (1.67x) vs MKL at kernel level -- SpMV is a primary named member of the evaluated family.

spmv|conf/sc/DuLWLTS22.regime: general SuiteSparse Matrix Collection (843 matrices), CPU/ARM
spmv|conf/sc/DuLWLTS22.rationale: AlphaSparse's headline is auto-generating novel SpMV formats/kernels per input matrix, evaluated at kernel level against 5 SOTA hand-designed formats plus autotuning baselines across SuiteSparse.

spmv|conf/sc/LuZWFLCY0C024.regime: tensor-core mixed-precision SpMV inside AMG V-cycle (level-dependent fp64/fp32/fp16 cascade), workload-weighted over solver levels
spmv|conf/sc/LuZWFLCY0C024.rationale: AmgT's SpMV kernel is real and separately instrumented (time_spmv) but per benchspecs/spmv/survey.md, it is evaluated embedded in the AMG solve phase (up to 1,551 calls/run) rather than as an isolated kernel benchmark; overlaps the sequence-krylov variant's usage pattern but at mixed/lower precision.

spmv|conf/sc/QiuXFZD0WCC024.regime: structurally+numerically symmetric SuiteSparse subset (rows>5e4, nnz>1e5), fp; x86/ARM CPU
spmv|conf/sc/QiuXFZD0WCC024.rationale: DCS-SpMV's headline is exactly a symmetric-SpMV divide-and-conquer algorithm evaluated at kernel level vs SOTA on x86/ARM; its own criterion defines the spec's spmv-symmetric-kernel variant. CPU-only.

spmv|journals/tpds/AhmadYU21.regime: SpMV used only as a residual/correction sub-step inside an SpTRSV DAG split, SuiteSparse triangular matrices
spmv|journals/tpds/AhmadYU21.rationale: The paper's contribution is a split-execution model for SpTRSV; SpMV appears only as a byproduct term of the DAG split (one of two sub-solves plus an SpMV), never independently optimized or benchmarked as a standalone kernel.

spmv|journals/tpds/AzadSHGB22.rationale: CombBLAS 2.0 is a general distributed-memory combinatorial-algorithms library; SpMV is one of many primitives, evaluated mainly via scaling/application benchmarks across the whole library rather than isolated kernel-vs-vendor-library throughput -- hardest call in this group since GPU kernel support exists but is not the paper's evaluation focus.

spmv|journals/tpds/LiAY21.regime: SuiteSparse-class matrices with varied input-vector sparsity (SpMV/SpMSpV), GPU
spmv|journals/tpds/LiAY21.rationale: Headline is an adaptive ML-based kernel-selection framework specifically for SpMV/SpMSpV evaluated at kernel level on GPUs; emphasis on varied vector sparsity is narrower than the spec's plain dense-vector SpMV variant.

sptrsv|conf/ipps/ZarebavaniCLSD22.rationale: Explicitly named as one of two papers (with partially-strided-codelet) whose analysis/scheduling algorithm IS the contribution, anchoring the spec's sptrsv-analysis-phase variant. CPU only.

sptrsv|conf/sc/01790S0L23.regime: distributed 3D communication-avoiding SpTRSV, real LU-factorization fill-in matrices (nlpkkt80, Ga19As19H42, ldoor), up to 256 GPUs
sptrsv|conf/sc/01790S0L23.rationale: Explicitly the sole track anchor for the spec's sptrsv-distributed-scaling variant (SC'23 Table-1 matrices used verbatim); headline scope is inherently multi-node/multi-GPU, not a single-GPU path.

sptrsv|conf/sc/CheshmiCD22.regime: SuiteSparse matrices, CPU vectorized SpMV/SpMM/SpTRSV via codelet mining, vs MKL/Sympiler
sptrsv|conf/sc/CheshmiCD22.rationale: SpTRSV is one of the paper's three directly kernel-level-benchmarked targets (vs MKL and vs Sympiler specifically for SpTRSV); explicitly named alongside HDagg as an analysis-phase anchor paper.

sptrsv|journals/tpds/AhmadYU21.rationale: Split_SpTRSV's headline IS an SpTRSV algorithm evaluated on the SuiteSparse Matrix Collection at the scale the spec's sptrsv-solve-kernel variant targets, explicitly referenced in the spec.

sptrsv|journals/tpds/ZhangSLHWDW21.regime: 245 SuiteSparse matrices, GPU sync-free thread+warp-fused SpTRSV vs cuSPARSE
sptrsv|journals/tpds/ZhangSLHWDW21.rationale: Explicitly named in the spec's sptrsv-solve-kernel variant as the anchor for the ~245-matrix scale; headline IS a GPU SpTRSV kernel evaluated against cuSPARSE.

sssp|conf/cgo/ZhangBCDKAS20.regime: standard graph benchmarks including road networks with large diameters, CPU, SSSP is one of six ordered graph algorithms generated by the DSL
sssp|conf/cgo/ZhangBCDKAS20.rationale: GraphIt's priority/bucket-fusion extension is a DSL that generates and optimizes several ordered graph algorithms (SSSP among them); comparisons are against Julienne/Galois/GAPBS on the standard ordered-algorithm benchmark set.

sssp|conf/ipps/GeraK23.regime: large real-world graphs compressed via Elias-Fano encoding (primarily unweighted for BFS); SSSP and PageRank are stated extensions, not the depth-evaluated algorithm
sssp|conf/ipps/GeraK23.rationale: The paper's headline contribution is a GPU-decompressible graph compression format evaluated in depth via BFS; SSSP is explicitly an added extension ('we also extend our work to...'), so it is a downstream application of the compression kernel rather than the headline SSSP algorithm, and its base format targets unweighted graphs.

sssp|conf/ppopp/WangFL21.regime: weighted directed graphs, GPU steady-state SSSP kernel, novel approximate priority-queue scheduler
sssp|conf/ppopp/WangFL21.rationale: Headline IS a GPU SSSP algorithm evaluated at kernel level against prior GPU SSSP work, exactly the spec's kernel-weighted-static variant.

stencil|conf/cgo/AlappatSHKRW21.regime: stencil kernels arising from explicit ODE-method discretizations, ECM-performance-model-guided autotuning, CPU (Cascade Lake/Rome); overlap with the named star/box catalog not confirmed
stencil|conf/cgo/AlappatSHKRW21.rationale: Headline is a stencil-optimization/performance-prediction tool built directly on Intel's YASK stencil framework, reporting measured gains from ECM-guided kernel selection -- matches variant 1's CPU general-compute class conceptually, but the specific ODE-derived shapes weren't confirmed against the named shape catalog.

stencil|conf/cgo/KoehlerS21.regime: single-pass Harris corner-detection image pipeline (Sobel gradients + structure tensor), fixed 2-image evaluation set, ARM mobile CPU, no time-stepping
stencil|conf/cgo/KoehlerS21.rationale: Harris corner detection is a one-shot 2D image-filter pipeline, not the track's iterative T-time-step PDE stencil sweep; this paper is the sole subject of its own dedicated morphology-image-kernel track, so its assignment here looks like an over-generalization of 'neighborhood-weighted-sum operation' rather than a genuine PDE-stencil match.

stencil|conf/cgo/LichtKMBHH21.regime: general stencil-DAG programs (including a production weather-simulation stencil) mapped to FPGA spatial hardware, single- and multi-device, TOp/s
stencil|conf/cgo/LichtKMBHH21.rationale: Headline contribution is entirely stencil-DAG-to-hardware mapping, evaluated at kernel level (TOp/s) -- the whole paper is about stencils, matching 'core'; but FPGA device class and heterogeneous-DAG framing differ from the CPU/GPU shape/grid convention, though the spec's own variant-1 digest cites sibling FPGA paper StencilsOnFPGA as informing the same general-purpose-compute class.

stencil|conf/cgo/MatsumuraZWEM20.regime: synthetic star/box 2D/3D stencils plus named application kernels, fp64 (fp32 secondary), single V100/P100, degree-10 temporal blocking
stencil|conf/cgo/MatsumuraZWEM20.rationale: AN5D originates the star/box shape-naming convention the whole track reuses verbatim and is the primary defining paper for variant 1's protocol (400ms floor, 5 reps + discarded warmup).

stencil|conf/dac/SchefflerCB24.regime: various stencil codes on an 8-core RISC-V compute cluster (Snitch) with indirect stream registers; precision/shape convention unconfirmed, plus an extrapolated 256-core projection not measured hardwar
stencil|conf/dac/SchefflerCB24.rationale: Headline is stencil-acceleration hardware (indirect stream registers) evaluated at kernel level (speedup, FPU utilization) against an RV32G baseline -- same general-purpose-compute class as variant 1, but this paper wasn't in the depth survey and its shape/precision convention could not be checked against the named star/box catalog, so only partial confidence in suite overlap.

stencil|conf/ics/ZhangWCMWEM23.rationale: PERKS is explicitly named as one of the papers defining variant 1's 'common denominator'; reports kernel-level GCells/s, GFLOPS, and bandwidth against SOTA libraries.

stencil|conf/ipps/BisbasLLNGK21.regime: 3D finite-difference wave-propagation stencils (isotropic/anisotropic acoustic, elastic), fp32, CPU (Broadwell/Skylake), CFL-determined iteration counts
stencil|conf/ipps/BisbasLLNGK21.rationale: Explicitly named as one of variant 1's defining papers ('Devito's generated code'); ablates temporal blocking against Devito's own spatially-blocked baseline at kernel level (GPoints/s).

stencil|conf/ipps/KamalavasanMRF21.regime: Poisson-5pt/Jacobi-7pt/RTM-25pt stencils, fp32, Xilinx Alveo U280 FPGA, on-chip-capacity-limited grid sizes vs a V100 GPU energy/runtime comparison
stencil|conf/ipps/KamalavasanMRF21.rationale: Headline is entirely an FPGA stencil-accelerator design workflow, evaluated at kernel level (GB/s, runtime); explicitly named alongside AN5D/PERKS as informing variant 1's design and its rtm3d25p8th shape is folded into variant 1's own recommended_subset, but its own grid sizes (50^3-400^2) are far smaller than the CPU/GPU convention and the spec reports it separately by design.

stencil|conf/ipps/YaoZLX26.regime: full shallow-water dynamical core (HOPE) on the Williamson standard test suite, Ozaki-scheme fp16 Tensor Cores emulating fp64 accuracy, single NVIDIA GPU (A40/RTX A6000)
stencil|conf/ipps/YaoZLX26.rationale: Headline is the Ozaki-scheme TCU stencil reformulation itself, and this paper is the explicit worked example for the spec's e2e-application variant (Williamson geostrophic-flow case named verbatim in its recommended_subset).

stencil|conf/ppopp/ChenLWBWMYZCY24.regime: 1D/2D/3D stencil-as-matmul on Tensor Cores, fp16-class, single A100, kernel microbenchmark
stencil|conf/ppopp/ChenLWBWMYZCY24.rationale: ConvStencil originates the shape/CLI catalog and bulk-timing idiom the whole TCU-matmul variant reuses verbatim; kernel-level GStencil/s vs cuDNN im2col baseline.

stencil|conf/ppopp/GuW0Y26.regime: 1D/2D stencil-as-sparse-matmul on Sparse Tensor Cores, fp16, single A100, kernel microbenchmark
stencil|conf/ppopp/GuW0Y26.rationale: SPIDER is one of the four papers whose shared CLI/shape catalog literally defines the TCU-matmul variant; reports kernel-level GStencil/s vs cuDNN/ConvStencil/LoRAStencil/FlashFFTStencil with preprocessing excluded and measured separately, exactly the variant's protocol.

stencil|conf/ppopp/HanLCBZYCZCY25.regime: 1D/2D/3D stencil via FFT-bridged Tensor-Core matmul, fp16, A100/H100, kernel microbenchmark
stencil|conf/ppopp/HanLCBZYCZCY25.rationale: FlashFFTStencil shares the ConvStencil/LoRAStencil/SPIDER CLI/timing convention that defines the TCU-matmul variant; headline 2.57x average kernel-level speedup over prior SOTA.

stencil|conf/sc/BrunnHBMM20.regime: high-order finite-difference operators (interpolation/gradient/divergence) embedded in a Gauss-Newton-Krylov image-registration solver, fp64/fp32, multi-GPU with a single-V100 number reported
stencil|conf/sc/BrunnHBMM20.rationale: The FD stencil operators are one part of a larger nonlinear image-registration optimization pipeline (interpolation+FD+FFT+Krylov solve), not an isolated iterative PDE sweep; a genuine single-V100 256^3-in-5s number exists but the operators are single-application inside a much larger solver stack.

stencil|conf/sc/FernandoNHZSGB22.regime: adaptive-mesh-refinement (octree) finite-difference update inside a full multi-GPU numerical-relativity solver, fp64; weak/strong scaling to hundreds of GPUs, with a single-A100 point (800 GFlops/s) a
stencil|conf/sc/FernandoNHZSGB22.rationale: The FD stencil update is one part of a much larger AMR gravitational-wave solver and is evaluated end-to-end (whole-simulation speedup/scaling), not as an isolated kernel; adaptive octree grids are also a structurally different regime than the spec's dense D-dimensional grid.

stencil|conf/sc/MunksgaardHSO22.regime: Rodinia Hotspot 2D thermal-diffusion stencil benchmark at its standard problem size, single NVIDIA GPU; one of three unrelated Rodinia kernels (LUD, Hotspot, NW) generated by a general array-language

stencil|conf/sc/ZhangLYCZCY24.regime: 1D/2D/3D stencil-as-matmul on Tensor Cores (low-rank weight decomposition), fp16-class, single A100, kernel microbenchmark
stencil|conf/sc/ZhangLYCZCY24.rationale: LoRAStencil is explicitly named alongside ConvStencil/FlashFFTStencil/SPIDER as defining the TCU-matmul variant's shared CLI and shape catalog.

stencil|journals/tpds/GreteGO21.rationale: Explicitly named as variant 1's defining example ('K-Athena's core update kernel'); reports a clean single-GPU cell-updates/s number (>10^8 on one V100) alongside its production-application framing.

stencil|journals/tpds/LichtBMH21.rationale: This is a general transformation catalog, not a stencil-specific contribution -- stencil is one of several example kernels used to demonstrate the taxonomy, evaluated on FPGA rather than the CPU/GPU convention.

string-regex-matching|conf/asplos/0002PJ.rationale: Headline IS a GPU NFA-matching kernel optimization (read privatization, dynamic load balancing) evaluated at kernel-level throughput against both software and hardware (Automata Processor) baselines.

string-regex-matching|conf/asplos/GeZ024.rationale: Headline IS a GPU automata-processing kernel technique (non-blocking symbol processing), evaluated as precompiled-automaton steady-state throughput, exactly the precompiled-kernel variant.

string-regex-matching|conf/cgo/SomainiCA.rationale: The MLIR dialects target only regex matching (not a multi-kernel general compiler); this is a compilation-technique paper whose contribution is squarely regex-matching codegen, matching the compilation-amortized variant's description.

string-regex-matching|conf/ipps/WangWQW2.regime: real-world FSM workloads, GPU steady-state matching throughput vs SOTA GPU FSM parallelization
string-regex-matching|conf/ipps/WangWQW2.rationale: Headline IS a GPU FSM/regex-matching parallelization technique (speculation-centric scheduling) benchmarked at kernel-level throughput.

vertex-cover|conf/ipps/YamoutBJMH22.rationale: This paper's GPU search-tree traversal for Minimum/Parameterized Vertex Cover is the sole and direct basis for both variants of this track.
